# QVF kind catalogue

This page lists every canonical section kind of QVF version 1, in the order of `registry.json`. It is generated from the [schema](../spec/qvf_manifest.schema.json), the [registry](../registry.json) and the [conformance corpus](../conformance/corpus); the [specification](../spec/qvf-format-spec.md) is normative and wins where this summary is shorter. Regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_kinds.py` (`--check` fails on drift).

Every section also carries the common fields of `$defs/Section`:

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | string | Unique identifier for this section within the file. |
| `kind` | yes | string | Kind string from the QVF registry or x_<vendor>.* namespace. |
| `label` |  | string |  |
| `component` |  | string |  |
| `critical` |  | boolean | If true, a consumer that does not support this kind MUST refuse to open the archive; see QVF spec § 7.4 (Root extensions block and per-section critical). |
| `structure_ref` |  | string | Id of the `structure` section this section describes. It must name a section of kind `structure` in this archive. When one of the section's payloads also carries a `structure_ref` (the `basis` of a `wavefunction.gto`), this one takes precedence; see QVF spec § 4.1 (Section object). |
| `run_ref` |  | string | Id of the `run.record` section of the program run that produced this section. It must name a section of kind `run.record` in this archive; see QVF spec § 4.1 (Section object). |
| `group` |  | string | Free-text label that groups related sections for display, e.g. 'step 2: frequencies'. Sections with equal `group` values belong together; the value carries no other meaning; see QVF spec § 4.1 (Section object). |
| `members` | yes | object |  |

Member formats: *json* is a JSON member checked against its payload definition, *binary* is a raw little-endian array with the listed dtypes and rank, *opaque* is a binary member without a dtype.

<a id="kind-structure"></a>

## `structure`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionStructure`.

Atoms plus an optional cell. The `structure` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/StructurePayload` and the optional `bonds` member's by `#/$defs/BondsPayload`; because they are archive members rather than manifest content, a validator checks them separately from manifest.json; see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds) and § 6 (Validation semantics). The optional biomolecule fields (`chains`, `residues`, `secondary_structure`, `b_factors`) sit on this section object rather than in the payload, and are independently optional: a structure carrying none of them is a valid plain structure, and a consumer that does not understand them ignores them. So do the optional fields of the species' chemical identity (`charge`, `multiplicity`, `name`, `smiles`, `inchi`, `inchikey`; the generic `label` is its compound label); see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity.

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `structure` | yes | json |  |  | [`StructurePayload`](#def-structurepayload) |
| `bonds` |  | json |  |  | [`BondsPayload`](#def-bondspayload) |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chains` |  | array of string | Chain ids present in this structure, in the order a consumer should present them. OPTIONAL and additive. |
| `residues` |  | array of [`BiomoleculeResidue`](#def-biomoleculeresidue) | Residue decomposition of the structure, in chain order. OPTIONAL and additive. A consumer that can also derive residues from per-atom fields MUST prefer these when present. |
| `secondary_structure` |  | array of [`BiomoleculeSecondaryStructure`](#def-biomoleculesecondarystructure) | Per-chain secondary-structure ranges. OPTIONAL and additive; takes precedence over a consumer's own geometric assignment. |
| `b_factors` |  | array of number | One temperature factor per atom, parallel to the `structure` payload's `atoms` order. OPTIONAL and additive. A consumer MUST ignore the array entirely when its length differs from the atom count, rather than assigning a partial mapping; and per-atom `StructureAtom.b_factor`, where present, wins over this array. |
| `charge` |  | integer | Net charge of the species whose atoms the `structure` payload holds, in units of the elementary charge. Absent states nothing (not neutral). With the payload's atomic numbers it gives the electron count, which must not be negative; in an archive with one `structure` section it must equal `provenance.charge` when both are present. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity. |
| `multiplicity` |  | integer | Spin multiplicity 2S+1 of the species. With `charge`, multiplicity − 1 must not exceed the electron count and must have its parity; in an archive with one `structure` section it must equal `provenance.multiplicity` when both are present. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity. |
| `name` |  | string | Name of the species, e.g. 'ethanol'. The generic `label` is the short label a scheme shows, such as a compound number. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity. |
| `smiles` |  | string | SMILES of the species, hydrogens implied or explicit. It names the species as a whole and implies no atom order. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity. |
| `inchi` |  | string | InChI of the species, standard ('InChI=1S/…') or not. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity. |
| `inchikey` |  | string | InChIKey of the species. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), under Chemical identity. |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/structure_periodic.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "structure",
  "kind": "structure",
  "members": {
    "structure": {
      "path": "structure/structure.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "4568c1f3e425fbd521cd67bb7c3335b59aec71b20adfa9fefd2701a84dcae9a0"
    }
  }
}
```

`structure` payload (`structure/structure.json`):

```json
{
  "atoms": [
    {
      "symbol": "Mg",
      "position": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
      "atomic_number": 12
    },
    {
      "symbol": "O",
      "position": [2.1, 2.1, 2.1],
      "atomic_number": 8
    }
  ],
  "pbc": [true, true, true],
  "lattice_vectors": [
    [4.2, 0.0, 0.0],
    [0.0, 4.2, 0.0],
    [0.0, 0.0, 4.2]
  ]
}
```

<a id="kind-bonds"></a>

## `bonds`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionBonds`.

Explicit connectivity of a structure as atom pairs. The `bonds` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/BondsPayload`, as is the optional `bonds` member of a `structure` section. The atom indices address the atoms of the structure the section's `structure_ref` names, else of the archive's first structure; an archive with several structures SHOULD set `structure_ref`. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bonds` | yes | json |  |  | [`BondsPayload`](#def-bondspayload) |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/bonds.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "bonds",
  "kind": "bonds",
  "members": {
    "bonds": {
      "path": "bonds/connectivity.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "c1c265ef181816cfa49c017cb94a77995fe6a7175f70c1ef56f0204cc27a3013"
    }
  }
}
```

`bonds` payload (`bonds/connectivity.json`):

```json
{
  "pairs": [
    {"i": 0, "j": 1, "order": 2.0},
    {"i": 0, "j": 2, "order": 1.0},
    {"i": 0, "j": 3}
  ]
}
```

## `bond_orders`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionBondOrders`.

Bond-order table — Mayer / Wiberg bond orders with atom-pair labels and distances. The `bond_orders` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/BondOrdersPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond_orders` | yes | json |  |  | [`BondOrdersPayload`](#def-bondorderspayload) |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/analysis.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "bond_orders",
  "kind": "bond_orders",
  "members": {
    "bond_orders": {
      "path": "bond_orders/orders.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "9bcd9b4cd3843ee74eb1f55b05cc4d0c5d5c841ff13b9d00a1c96fa44fd7e36b"
    }
  }
}
```

`bond_orders` payload (`bond_orders/orders.json`):

```json
{
  "method": "mayer",
  "pairs": [
    {"i": 0, "j": 1, "order": 0.98, "distance_ang": 0.96}
  ]
}
```

## `volume.difference`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionVolumeDifference`.

Difference density (or any difference scalar field). Structurally identical to volume.density; carries optional references to the two operand sections used to compute it. Sign convention: data = a - b.

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | yes | json |  |  | [`VolumeGridPayload`](#def-volumegridpayload) |
| `data` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 3 |  |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operand_a` |  | string | Section id of the minuend (the 'a' in a - b). Must reference a section that exists in this archive. |
| `operand_b` |  | string | Section id of the subtrahend (the 'b' in a - b). Must reference a section that exists in this archive. |
| `description` |  | string | Optional human-readable description, e.g. 'ρ(product) - ρ(reactant)'. |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/volume_difference.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "rho_diff",
  "kind": "volume.difference",
  "members": {
    "grid": {
      "path": "volumes/rho_diff_grid.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "4ca62544cbd7c00e006423c5b617e8cf02150dacc82f7643e4cf5ef456c56d9a"
    },
    "data": {
      "path": "volumes/rho_diff.dat",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "79cfd24a0bbf62432e6619eea36ae8a368228957e94af82f7b92c58e911e319c",
      "dtype": "float32",
      "shape": [4, 4, 5]
    }
  },
  "label": "rho(A) - rho(B)",
  "operand_a": "rho_a",
  "operand_b": "rho_b",
  "description": "rho(A) - rho(B)"
}
```

`grid` payload (`volumes/rho_diff_grid.json`):

```json
{
  "origin": [-1.2000000000000002, -1.2000000000000002, -1.6],
  "voxel_vectors": [
    [0.8, 0.0, 0.0],
    [0.0, 0.8, 0.0],
    [0.0, 0.0, 0.8]
  ],
  "shape": [4, 4, 5]
}
```

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionVolumePotential`.

## `volume.generic`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionVolumeGeneric`.

Generic scalar field — escape hatch for any volumetric kind that doesn't map onto density/orbital/spin/elf/difference. Structurally identical: grid + data. Producers should prefer a more specific kind when one fits.

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | yes | json |  |  | [`VolumeGridPayload`](#def-volumegridpayload) |
| `data` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 3 |  |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/volume_generic.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

```json
{
  "id": "laplacian",
  "kind": "volume.generic",
  "members": {

    }

}

    [0.0, 0.0, 0.8]
  ],
  "shape": [4, 6, 5]
}
```

<a id="kind-volume-laplacian"></a>

## `volume.laplacian`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionVolumeLaplacian`.

Laplacian of the electron density, ∇²ρ, in e/bohr⁵: negative where charge concentrates, positive where it is depleted. Identical member structure to volume.density (grid + 3-D data). The vocabulary has no unit name for e/bohr⁵, so the grid does not declare `units.data` for it. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | yes | json |  |  | [`VolumeGridPayload`](#def-volumegridpayload) |
| `data` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 3 |  |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/volume_laplacian.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

```json

  "id": "lap",

    },

      "path": "volumes/lap.dat",

      "dtype": "float32",
      "shape": [5, 4, 6]
    }
  },
  "label": "Laplacian of the electron density"
}
```

`grid` payload (`volumes/lap_grid.json`):

```json
{
  "origin": [-1.4, -1.0499999999999998, -1.75],

<a id="kind-volume-vector"></a>

## `volume.vector`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionVolumeVector`.

A Cartesian vector field on a grid, such as a density gradient, an electric field or a current density: `data` is [nx, ny, nz, 3] with the x, y and z components on the last axis, in the Cartesian frame of the grid `origin`. Its unit is that of the field, which the grid declares as `units.data` when the vocabulary names it. The section field `component` is not used. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | yes | json |  |  | [`VolumeGridPayload`](#def-volumegridpayload) |
| `data` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 4 |  |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/volume_vector.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

    },

      "path": "volumes/grad_rho.dat",
      "format": "binary",

      "dtype": "float32",
      "shape": [4, 5, 6, 3]
    }
  },
  "label": "Density gradient"
}
```

`grid` payload (`volumes/grad_rho_grid.json`):

```json

  "origin": [-1.2000000000000002, -1.6, -2.0],

<a id="kind-volume-series"></a>

## `volume.series`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionVolumeSeries`.

A series of n scalar fields on one grid, indexed by time, trajectory frame, electronic state or another quantity: `data` is [n, nx, ny, nz], slab s holding the field at the axis value `axis.values[s]`, and the required `axis` member says what the leading axis is. It supersedes, without deprecating, the `frame_volumes` + `volume_grid` members of a `reaction.path` section. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | yes | json |  |  | [`VolumeGridPayload`](#def-volumegridpayload) |
| `data` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 4 |  |
| `axis` | yes | json |  |  | [`VolumeSeriesAxisPayload`](#def-volumeseriesaxispayload) |

<a id="kind-wavefunction-gto"></a>

## `wavefunction.gto`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionWavefunctionGTO`.

Atom-centered Gaussian basis + MO coefficients. Renderer-friendly: a re-sampling viewer can evaluate any orbital on its own grid (Molden-style). Complex coefficients are stored as float64 [n_mo, n_ao, 2] with last axis [real, imag]. Optional AO-basis matrices: the `overlap` matrix, with which a consumer verifies the normalization contract of QVF spec Appendix A.1, and the one-particle density matrices `density_matrix` (with `mo_coefficients`) or `density_matrix_alpha` + `density_matrix_beta` (with the α and β coefficients). See QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `basis` | yes | json |  |  | [`BasisPayload`](#def-basispayload) |
| `mo_metadata` | yes | json |  |  | [`MoMetadataPayload`](#def-mometadatapayload) |
| `mo_coefficients` |  | binary | `float64` | 2–3 |  |
| `mo_coefficients_alpha` |  | binary | `float64` | 2–3 |  |
| `mo_coefficients_beta` |  | binary | `float64` | 2–3 |  |
| `overlap` |  | binary | `float64` | 2 |  |
| `density_matrix` |  | binary | `float64` | 2 |  |
| `density_matrix_alpha` |  | binary | `float64` | 2 |  |
| `density_matrix_beta` |  | binary | `float64` | 2 |  |

      "path": "wf/basis.json",

<a id="kind-wavefunction-bloch"></a>

## `wavefunction.bloch`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionWavefunctionBloch`.

Provisional kind. The k-resolved Bloch orbitals of a periodic system over the atom-centred Gaussian basis of its cell: complex MO coefficients at every k-point of a set, for one or two spin channels, with their energies and occupations. The Bloch functions are phi_mu,k(r) = N^(-1/2) sum_T exp(+i k.T) chi_mu(r - T) over the lattice translations T, with k in fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates and the AO order and primitive normalization of QVF spec Appendix A. The structure named by the section-level structure_ref, else by basis.structure_ref, must have at least one periodic axis; validators check that and the agreement of the member shapes. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `basis` | yes | json |  |  | [`BasisPayload`](#def-basispayload) |
| `kpoints` | yes | json |  |  | [`BlochKpointsPayload`](#def-blochkpointspayload) |
| `mo_metadata` | yes | json |  |  | [`BlochMoMetadataPayload`](#def-blochmometadatapayload) |
| `mo_coefficients` | yes | binary | `float64` | 5 |  |
| `energies` | yes | binary | `float64` | 3 |  |
| `occupations` | yes | binary | `float64` | 3 |  |

<a id="kind-atom-properties"></a>

## `atom_properties`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionAtomProperties`.

Per-atom analysis results. The member roles are the one canonical role list: the scalar roles `mulliken_charge`, `loewdin_charge`, `hirshfeld_charge`, `iao_charge`, `spin_population`, `cm5_charge`, `chelpg_charge`, `resp_charge`, `esp_charge`, `nbo_charge`, `mbis_charge`, `bader_charge`, `ddec_charge`, `valence`, `bonded_valence`, `fukui_plus`, `fukui_minus`, `fukui_zero`, `dual_descriptor`, `atomic_energy_eh`, `atomic_volume_bohr3`, `nmr_shielding_iso_ppm`, each float64 [n_atoms], and the vector roles `magnetic_moment` and `force_eh_bohr`, each float64 [n_atoms, 3]. A section carries one or more of them, plus any number of `custom.<name>` roles (scalar or vector), which are allowed only together with a `meta` member that describes each of them. Specified in QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

| `ddec_charge` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |
| `valence` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |
| `bonded_valence` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |
| `fukui_plus` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |

<a id="kind-trajectory"></a>

## `trajectory`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionTrajectory`.

A sequence of frames of one set of atoms: an optimization, an IRC, a scan, a NEB or a molecular-dynamics run. `metadata` names the atoms and `coords` holds the positions; the optional members add per-frame data: the cell (`lattice`, rows in Angstrom), `velocities`, the energy `gradient` (the forces are its negative), `times`, `energies`, `cell_volumes` and `temperatures`. Every per-frame member has the leading extent of `coords`. See QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata` | yes | json |  |  | [`TrajectoryMetadataPayload`](#def-trajectorymetadatapayload) |
| `coords` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 3 |  |
| `lattice` |  | binary | `float64` | 2–3 |  |
| `velocities` |  | binary | `float64` | 3 |  |
| `gradient` |  | binary | `float64` | 3 |  |
| `times` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |
| `energies` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |
| `cell_volumes` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |
| `temperatures` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/trajectory.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "opt",

    "metadata": {
      "path": "opt/metadata.json",

    },

      "shape": [4, 3, 3]
    }
  }
}
```

{
  "symbols": ["O", "H", "H"],

  "n_frames": 4,

<a id="kind-reaction-path"></a>

## `reaction.path`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionReactionPath`.

Self-contained reaction path: frames + per-frame energies + waypoint annotations identifying reactant / transition state / intermediate / product frames. Binary layout matches `trajectory` so the same readers can decode coords. Optional per-frame volumetric data (electron density / an orbital morphing along the path) may be attached via the `frame_volumes` (4D: [n_emitted_frames, nx, ny, nz]) + `volume_grid` members; the metadata then carries `volume_frame_index` (which path frame each emitted slab belongs to, for decimation), `volume_label`, and optional `volume_isovalue`. Readers that don't understand these members ignore them. These two members are the older form of a `volume.series` section whose `axis` has kind `frame` and names the path, which producers should prefer; both stay valid. The optional `velocities`, `gradient`, `times` and `energies` members carry per-frame data with the shapes and units they have in a trajectory, and the optional `lattice` member (columns, bohr) marks the path periodic; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata` | yes | json |  |  | [`ReactionPathMetadataPayload`](#def-reactionpathmetadatapayload) |
| `coords` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 3 |  |
| `frame_volumes` |  | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 4 |  |
| `volume_grid` |  | json |  |  | [`VolumeGridPayload`](#def-volumegridpayload) |
| `lattice` |  | binary | `float64` | 2–3 |  |
| `velocities` |  | binary | `float64` | 3 |  |
| `gradient` |  | binary | `float64` | 3 |  |
| `times` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |
| `energies` |  | binary | `float64` | 1 |  |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/reaction_path.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "rxn",
  "kind": "reaction.path",
  "members": {
    "metadata": {
      "path": "rxn/metadata.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "c3d3e6cfc58d72efe283f877cf5838dc55f21e1f10affa34f14f036335c45f79"
    },
    "coords": {
      "path": "rxn/coords.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "1dac483807ac226f521bc8eb5c1fb4e2b4b9147eb1d3a35c109e3edad14df0f6",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [5, 3, 3]
    }
  }
}
```

`metadata` payload (`rxn/metadata.json`):

```json
{
  "symbols": ["C", "N", "H"],
  "atomic_numbers": [6, 7, 1],
  "energies": [-93.19, -93.15, -93.115, -93.152, -93.166],
  "kind": "irc",
  "reaction_coordinate": [-2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0],
  "reaction_coordinate_label": "IRC arc length",
  "reaction_coordinate_unit": "bohr",
  "waypoints": [
    {"frame_index": 0, "label": "HCN", "kind": "reactant", "energy_eh": -93.19},
    {"frame_index": 2, "label": "TS", "kind": "transition_state", "energy_eh": -93.115},
    {"frame_index": 4, "label": "HNC", "kind": "product", "energy_eh": -93.166}
  ]
}
```

<a id="kind-reaction-waypoints"></a>

## `reaction.waypoints`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionReactionWaypoints`.

Lightweight waypoint annotations layered onto an existing `trajectory` section. Use this when the frames are already carried by a trajectory and you only want to label reactant/TS/intermediate/product frames without duplicating coords.

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `waypoints` | yes | json |  |  | [`ReactionWaypointsPayload`](#def-reactionwaypointspayload) |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trajectory_ref` | yes | string | Section id of the trajectory section this annotation refers to. Must reference an existing section with kind 'trajectory' in this archive. |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/trajectory.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "opt_marks",
  "kind": "reaction.waypoints",
  "trajectory_ref": "opt",
  "members": {
    "waypoints": {
      "path": "opt_marks/waypoints.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "d194f2c1d83105905d1c25f98b8ef0018e9c8e59564485cf3f29eb6538d7e01d"
    }
  }
}
```

`waypoints` payload (`opt_marks/waypoints.json`):

```json
{
  "waypoints": [
    {"frame_index": 0, "label": "start", "kind": "point", "energy_eh": -74.958},
    {"frame_index": 3, "label": "minimum", "kind": "product", "energy_eh": -74.9659}
  ]
}
```

<a id="kind-scan-surface"></a>

## `scan.surface`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionScanSurface`.

2D relaxed-scan energy surface: two driven internal coordinates (axis_a x axis_b) with the relaxed energy at each grid node. `energies` is a 2D binary array [nA, nB]; `axis_a` / `axis_b` are the 1D coordinate values (bohr for bonds, radians for angles/dihedrals). The metadata carries per-axis label + unit. Optional `geometries` (4D-flattened [nA*nB, n_atoms, 3] in angstrom, row-major over (a, b)) lets a viewer show the relaxed structure at a clicked node.

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata` | yes | json |  |  | [`ScanSurfaceMetadataPayload`](#def-scansurfacemetadatapayload) |
| `axis_a` | yes | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | ≥ 1 |  |
| `axis_b` | yes | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | ≥ 1 |  |
| `energies` | yes | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | ≥ 1 |  |
| `geometries` |  | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | ≥ 1 |  |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/scan_surface.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "scan",
  "kind": "scan.surface",
  "members": {
    "metadata": {
      "path": "scan/metadata.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "655c6c7fe8fb0d0eb5ed91f213f5cce891d44a910d77118a74c7267ff255b277"
    },
    "axis_a": {
      "path": "scan/axis_a.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "c624c1d4781a6f12c8dcf46e5c79e9e2bd8b89101190188459a13ea9fa806f96",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [3]
    },
    "axis_b": {
      "path": "scan/axis_b.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "3c349780a126f744390621765d1fcfd8e0bac4a39e29e8b5675713e8d985a73c",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [2]
    },
    "energies": {
      "path": "scan/energies.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "5c2e52555a1363057bc5634db52df4ceed56f5e19c03899c38cd131bba0e6dd7",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [3, 2]
    },
    "geometries": {

    "label": "r(O-H1)",

<a id="kind-bands"></a>

## `bands`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionBands`.

Band structure — eigenvalues along a k-path, with optional Mulliken character projections (fat bands).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kpath` | yes | json |  |  | [`KpathPayload`](#def-kpathpayload) |
| `eigenvalues` | yes | binary | `float64` | 3 |  |
| `projections` |  | binary | `float64` | 3–4 |  |

<a id="kind-dos-total"></a>

## `dos.total`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionDOSTotal`.

Total density of states on an energy grid. Its metadata rides as optional fields on the section object (`n_spin`, `smearing`, `smearing_type`, `fermi_energy_ev`, `n_electrons`), not as members. Specified in QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `energies` | yes | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | ≥ 1 |  |
| `dos` | yes | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | ≥ 1 |  |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_spin` |  | one of `1` \| `2` | Number of spin channels: 1 (spin-unpolarized) or 2 (spin-polarized). OPTIONAL. |
| `smearing` |  | number | Width of the broadening applied to the DOS, in eV. OPTIONAL. |
| `smearing_type` |  | string | Name of the broadening function, for example "gaussian". OPTIONAL; free text in v1. |
| `fermi_energy_ev` |  | number | Fermi energy, in eV. OPTIONAL. |
| `n_electrons` |  | number | Number of electrons; may be fractional. OPTIONAL. |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/dos.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "dos_total",
  "kind": "dos.total",
  "members": {
    "energies": {
      "path": "dos/dos_total_energies.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "4058c845a711333020e85aeea141797b6f13cef77f3699f0c42a7b1d0546306e",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [7]
    },
    "dos": {
      "path": "dos/dos_total.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "23bc05f1acd62b20d6dda57e7bd9d7655a1107b949c8a86c551810589b0bf5d9",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [2, 7]
    }
  },
  "n_spin": 2,
  "smearing": 0.1,
  "smearing_type": "gaussian",
  "fermi_energy_ev": 5.2,
  "n_electrons": 16.0
}
```

<a id="kind-dos-projected"></a>

## `dos.projected`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionDOSProjected`.

Projected density of states on an energy grid. Its metadata rides as optional fields on the section object, as for dos.total, plus `channels`, which labels the projection rows. Specified in QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `energies` | yes | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | ≥ 1 |  |
| `projections` | yes | binary | `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` | 2–3 |  |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_spin` |  | one of `1` \| `2` | Number of spin channels: 1 (spin-unpolarized) or 2 (spin-polarized). OPTIONAL. |
| `smearing` |  | number | Width of the broadening applied to the DOS, in eV. OPTIONAL. |
| `smearing_type` |  | string | Name of the broadening function, for example "gaussian". OPTIONAL; free text in v1. |
| `fermi_energy_ev` |  | number | Fermi energy, in eV. OPTIONAL. |
| `n_electrons` |  | number | Number of electrons; may be fractional. OPTIONAL. |
| `channels` |  | array of object | One label object per projection row, in row order. OPTIONAL. Every item field is optional, and items may carry further fields. |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/dos.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "dos_projected",
  "kind": "dos.projected",
  "members": {
    "energies": {
      "path": "dos/dos_projected_energies.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "4058c845a711333020e85aeea141797b6f13cef77f3699f0c42a7b1d0546306e",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [7]
    },
    "projections": {
      "path": "dos/dos_projected_projections.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "834f74bf682263f8f88dda235c3e99f8dd5c078094c8c4f3e6c58f700cc0f0ce",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [2, 2, 7]
    }
  },
  "n_spin": 2,
  "channels": [
    {"atom": 0, "l": 0, "label": "Fe1-s"},
    {"atom": 0, "l": 2, "label": "Fe1-d"}
  ],
  "fermi_energy_ev": 5.2
}
```

<a id="kind-run-record"></a>

## `run.record`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionRunRecord`.

Self-contained record of one program invocation: the verbatim input handed to a quantum-chemistry code and/or the full log/output it produced, plus auxiliary attachments. `program` names the code the input/log belong to — which may differ from the root `source.program` when the archive was written by a converter. `input` and `log` are opaque binary members that MUST decode as UTF-8 text; `attachment.*` members carry arbitrary bytes described by the optional `files` index.

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input` |  | opaque |  |  |  |
| `log` |  | opaque |  |  |  |
| `files` |  | json |  |  | [`RunRecordFilesPayload`](#def-runrecordfilespayload) |
| `^attachment\.[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` (pattern) |  | opaque |  |  |  |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program` | yes | string | The program that consumed `input` / produced `log` (e.g. 'vibe-qc', 'orca'). Lowercase identifiers recommended. |
| `program_version` |  | string |  |
| `command` |  | string | Command line used to launch the run, as one string. |
| `exit_status` |  | integer |  |
| `started_utc` |  | string | Run start, ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. '2026-07-24T12:00:00Z'). |
| `finished_utc` |  | string | Run end, ISO 8601 UTC. |
| `sequence` |  | integer | Ordering index when an archive carries multiple run records (multi-step workflows). |
| `job_ref` |  | string | Id of the `job.spec` section this run executed. It must name a section of kind `job.spec` in this archive. In an archive with several `job.spec` sections (a job set) it is how a reader tells which job ran; see QVF spec § 5.8 (run.record — self-contained run records) and QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification), under Job sets. |
| `run_status` |  | one of `"running"` \| `"converged"` \| `"failed"` | Outcome of this run, with the meanings of the root provenance.run_status. In a job set it is the status of the job that `job_ref` names; see QVF spec § 5.8 (run.record — self-contained run records). |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/run_record.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "run_record",
  "kind": "run.record",
  "program": "democode",
  "members": {
    "input": {
      "path": "run_record/input.txt",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "7e0fece96e82fdacc3427d074d6ebd067a32e5f469dd00ee95fa805b643e8084"
    },
    "log": {
      "path": "run_record/log.txt",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "0e6729db1f52719ba414c4e0ee024a94454d7da863df9514598952f4ac9d30e0"
    },
    "attachment.geom": {
      "path": "run_record/attachments/geom",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "33329f0c90ab6952aada64ff73e9fc8377ccb8013b675fe7f268ac6be2d29d3f"
    },
    "files": {
      "path": "run_record/files.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "c45c30951fff66018219377c54689d6b97bd3f702eb5173981e32a8c72a2f32f"
    }
  },
  "program_version": "1.0.0",
  "command": "democode water.inp",
  "exit_status": 0,
  "started_utc": "2026-07-24T12:00:00Z",
  "finished_utc": "2026-07-24T12:00:41Z"
}
```

`files` payload (`run_record/files.json`):

```json
{
  "input": {"filename": "water.inp"},
  "log": {"filename": "water.out"},
  "attachment.geom": {"filename": "water.xyz", "media_type": "chemical/x-xyz"}
}
```

<a id="kind-job-spec"></a>

## `job.spec`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionJobSpec`.

Declarative specification of the calculation an archive requests — before, and independent of, any results it carries; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Together with a `structure` section it makes the archive an executable input: a runner reconstructs the job from the `spec` payload, executes it, and writes results plus a `run.record` back into the same container. The payload is declarative data, never code.

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | yes | json |  |  | [`JobSpecPayload`](#def-jobspecpayload) |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/job_spec.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "job_spec",
  "kind": "job.spec",
  "members": {
    "spec": {
      "path": "job_spec/spec.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "c9d48a4317b59450915a54a82caf8df595335ba32d278592079633e2e80ae662"
    }
  }
}
```

`spec` payload (`job_spec/spec.json`):

```json
{
  "job_type": "periodic",
  "method": "rks",
  "basis": "pob-tzvp-rev2",
  "functional": "pbe",
  "charge": 0,
  "multiplicity": 1,
  "kpoints": [4, 4, 4],
  "tasks": ["single_point"],
  "options": {"cutoff_ha": 300.0}
}
```

<a id="kind-forces"></a>

## `forces`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionForces`.

First derivatives of the energy at one geometry: the nuclear energy gradient (the forces are its negative) and, for a periodic system, the stress. The gradient rows follow the atoms of the structure named by the section-level structure_ref when present, else by meta.structure_ref, else of the archive's only structure section. See QVF spec § 5.10 (forces — nuclear gradient and stress).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gradient` | yes | binary | `float64` | 2 |  |
| `stress` |  | binary | `float64` | 2 |  |
| `meta` |  | json |  |  | [`ForcesMetaPayload`](#def-forcesmetapayload) |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/forces_hessian.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "forces",
  "kind": "forces",
  "members": {
    "gradient": {
      "path": "forces/gradient.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "382d9f983a9e79c4c5d606fb1de3615a9aa39fcb37de554ec48c4137e345eb97",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [3, 3]
    },
    "meta": {
      "path": "forces/meta.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "dd81c44b335bc42041f0f3fb8cdb488f17e83adba001d27b98520172fe620070"
    }
  }
}
```

`meta` payload (`forces/meta.json`):

```json
{
  "structure_ref": "structure",
  "method": "rhf",
  "convention": "gradient",
  "units": {"energy": "hartree", "length": "bohr"}
}
```

<a id="kind-hessian"></a>

## `hessian`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionHessian`.

Second derivatives of the energy with respect to the nuclear Cartesian coordinates at one geometry. The atoms are resolved as for a forces section. See QVF spec § 5.11 (hessian — Cartesian second derivatives).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `matrix` | yes | binary | `float64` | 2 |  |
| `meta` |  | json |  |  | [`HessianMetaPayload`](#def-hessianmetapayload) |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/forces_hessian.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "hessian",
  "kind": "hessian",
  "members": {
    "matrix": {
      "path": "hessian/matrix.bin",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "84e428731c134706f6cd563e6df7d8c2772ea4a4186822588c9a2ef316908a5b",
      "dtype": "float64",
      "shape": [9, 9]
    },
    "meta": {
      "path": "hessian/meta.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "91fe744ed70843727f2c89b64067b9bdf251b3bb41718d78264667231dc4e62d"
    }
  }
}
```

`meta` payload (`hessian/meta.json`):

```json
{
  "structure_ref": "structure",
  "mass_weighted": false,
  "projected": false,
  "atom_masses_amu": [15.999, 1.008, 1.008],
  "units": {"energy": "hartree", "length": "bohr"}
}
```

<a id="kind-excited-states"></a>

## `excited_states`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionExcitedStates`.

Electronically excited states of one calculation (TD-DFT, CIS, ADC, EOM-CC and similar methods): a table of states with their excitation energies, transition properties and dominant orbital excitations, in the JSON member `states`, whose payload is `#/$defs/ExcitedStatesPayload`. A state may name its natural transition orbitals and its transition or difference density. See QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `states` | yes | json |  |  | [`ExcitedStatesPayload`](#def-excitedstatespayload) |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wavefunction_ref` |  | string | Id of the `wavefunction.gto` section of the reference state, usually the ground state, whose orbitals the `from_mo` and `to_mo` of the contributions index. It must name a section of kind `wavefunction.gto` in this archive; see QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties). |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/nto_unrestricted_empty_beta.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "es",
  "kind": "excited_states",
  "members": {
    "states": {
      "path": "es/states.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "fff3be5e568ff82f71a348d3fa665c1e21d2d75791df7c988d96cb74277bf4dc",
      "size": 161
    }
  }
}
```

`states` payload (`es/states.json`):

```json
{
  "states": [
    {
      "index": 1,
      "excitation_energy": {"value": 4.0, "units": "ev"},
      "nto_ref": "nto_hole"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="kind-volume-transition-density"></a>

## `volume.transition_density`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionVolumeTransitionDensity`.

Transition density of one electronic excitation on a grid: the one-particle transition density between the reference state and an excited state, summed over spin, in e/bohr^3. Same members as volume.density (grid + data); its overall sign is arbitrary. The optional section fields name the `excited_states` section and the state. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | yes | json |  |  | [`VolumeGridPayload`](#def-volumegridpayload) |
| `data` | yes | binary | `float32`, `float64` | 3 |  |

**Section fields**

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `excited_states_ref` |  | string | Id of the `excited_states` section the state belongs to. It must name a section of kind `excited_states` in this archive; see QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties). |
| `state_index` |  | integer | The `index` of the state whose transition density this is, in the `excited_states` section that `excited_states_ref` names, which is then required. |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/tddft.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "tden_s1",
  "kind": "volume.transition_density",
  "members": {
    "grid": {
      "path": "volumes/tden_s1_grid.json",
      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "2edd5e298d91f43115a0aa3c0e412da3542732b38401530c57fedc491eba2f01"
    },
    "data": {
      "path": "volumes/tden_s1.dat",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "664a7bde155a45e44d60ab8951e3f30c6024c70077fd18ed8bef4a4eedfc70d4",
      "dtype": "float32",
      "shape": [8, 10, 8]
    }
  },
  "label": "S1 transition density",
  "excited_states_ref": "excited_states",
  "state_index": 1
}
```

`grid` payload (`volumes/tden_s1_grid.json`):

```json
{
  "origin": [-1.75, -2.25, -2.25],
  "voxel_vectors": [
    [0.5, 0.0, 0.0],
    [0.0, 0.5, 0.0],
    [0.0, 0.0, 0.5]
  ],
  "shape": [8, 10, 8]
}
```

## `properties.electric`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionPropertiesElectric`.

Electric multipole moments and polarizabilities of the system: the dipole, quadrupole and octupole, and the polarizability and hyperpolarizability, each in the fixed unit of the spec. The single `properties` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/ElectricPropertiesPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `properties` | yes | json |  |  | [`ElectricPropertiesPayload`](#def-electricpropertiespayload) |

```json

  "kind": "properties.electric",

      "format": "json",
      "sha256": "3fe64ad23514fa8bea8d11f909c106a2b596c99a650035c3977b69fba39fa0d3"
    }
  }
}
```

`properties` payload (`electric/properties.json`):

  "origin": "center_of_mass",

    "units": "debye"
  },

      [-1.6145419736850657, 0.0, 0.0],

    ],
    "traceless": true,
    "convention": "buckingham"
  },
  "polarizability": {
    "matrix": [

}

The single `properties` member's JSON payload is specified by `#/$defs/DielectricPropertiesPayload`. The Born charges follow the atoms of the structure named by the section-level structure_ref when present, else of the archive's only structure section; see QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds).

}

```

<a id="kind-preview"></a>

## `preview`

Schema definition: `$defs/SectionPreview`.

A picture of the archive's contents for file managers, quick-look panels and catalogues: a raster `thumbnail` and an optional larger or vector `image`, both opaque binary members that carry their `media_type`. The picture of the archive is the thumbnail of the first `preview` section. An SVG image is self-contained and inert: no external resources, no scripts. See QVF spec § 5.15 (preview — a picture of the archive).

**Members**

| Role | Required | Format | dtypes | Rank | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `thumbnail` | yes | opaque |  |  |  |
| `image` |  | opaque |  |  |  |

**Example** (from `conformance/corpus/reaction_scheme.qvf`, long arrays shortened)

Manifest section:

```json
{
  "id": "preview",
  "kind": "preview",
  "label": "scheme",
  "members": {
    "thumbnail": {
      "path": "preview/thumbnail.png",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "c269d21b5f0a5b5eada1b5b74e34af408e0c92dfd717aff361c61f71b74360bf",
      "size": 105,
      "media_type": "image/png"
    },
    "image": {
      "path": "preview/image.svg",
      "format": "binary",
      "sha256": "0ad016f21198a53c8e19677ccc814118eb505beb1a7df92cc97406f17fa89c23",
      "size": 189,
      "media_type": "image/svg+xml"
    }
  }
}
```

## Payload definitions

The JSON payload definitions named in the member tables, in alphabetical order.

<a id="def-atompropertiesmetapayload"></a>

### `AtomPropertiesMetaPayload`

Used by: [`atom_properties`](#kind-atom-properties).

The JSON payload of the `meta` member of an `atom_properties` section: a map from the name of a `custom.<name>` role to its description. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only entries named by a `custom.<name>` role and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

<a id="def-basispayload"></a>

### `BasisPayload`

Used by: [`wavefunction.gto`](#kind-wavefunction-gto), [`wavefunction.bloch`](#kind-wavefunction-bloch).

The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.gto` section's `basis` member (conventionally `<section id>/basis.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The AO order is the concatenation of the shells in array order, each in the in-shell order of QVF spec Appendix A.2. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `structure_ref` | yes | string | Id of the `structure` section whose atoms the shell `center` indices refer to. |
| `pure` |  | boolean | Angular type of every shell without its own `pure`: true = spherical harmonics, false = Cartesian. Absent means true. |
| `n_ao` |  | integer | Number of AOs: the sum over the shells of 2l+1 (spherical) or (l+1)(l+2)/2 (Cartesian). It equals the AO dimension of the MO coefficient members. |
| `shells` | yes | array of [`BasisShell`](#def-basisshell) | The contracted shells, in AO order. |
| `ecp` |  | array of [`BasisEcpCentre`](#def-basisecpcentre) | Effective core potentials, at most one per atom (no two entries share a `center`); see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). |
| `n_electrons` |  | integer | Number of electrons the wavefunction describes: the sum of the atomic numbers, minus the `n_core_electrons` of every `ecp` entry, minus the charge. When present it equals the sum of the `mo_metadata` occupations over both spin channels (within 1e-6) and `provenance.n_electrons` when that is present; validators check both, which JSON Schema cannot express. |

<a id="def-blochkpointspayload"></a>

### `BlochKpointsPayload`

Used by: [`wavefunction.bloch`](#kind-wavefunction-bloch).

The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.bloch` section's `kpoints` member: the k-points the orbitals are given at, in the order of axis 0 of mo_coefficients, energies and occupations. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. That the arrays have one entry per k-point and that the weights sum to 1 within 1e-6 is checked by validators, not by this schema. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kpoints` | yes | array[1..] of array[3] of number | Every k-point, in fractional coordinates of the reciprocal lattice (k = k1 b1 + k2 b2 + k3 b3, so k.T = 2 pi (k1 n1 + k2 n2 + k3 n3) for the translation T = n1 a1 + n2 a2 + n3 a3). |
| `weights` |  | array of number | Integration weight of each k-point, one per entry of `kpoints`, summing to 1 within 1e-6. Absent when the k-points are not an integration set, such as points along a path. |
| `labels` |  | array of string | One label per k-point, parallel to `kpoints`, such as a high-symmetry name; an empty string marks an unlabelled point. |
| `mesh` |  | array[3] of integer | Dimensions [n1, n2, n3] of the uniform mesh the k-points were taken from, when they were; the k-points are its points, or the irreducible subset of them that the weights account for. |
| `shift` |  | array[3] of number | Fractional reciprocal-lattice position of mesh point (0, 0, 0). Absent means a Gamma-centred mesh. |
| `time_reversal` |  | boolean | True when the set was reduced with time-reversal symmetry: the orbitals at -k are the complex conjugates of those at k, and the weight of k includes that of -k. Absent means false. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional map from a field name of this payload to the unit name of its values. The fields are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions) and the payload table; a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `kpoints`, `weights` and `shift` are `dimensionless`. |

Fixed units: `kpoints` = `dimensionless`, `weights` = `dimensionless`, `shift` = `dimensionless`.

<a id="def-blochmometadatapayload"></a>

### `BlochMoMetadataPayload`

Used by: [`wavefunction.bloch`](#kind-wavefunction-bloch).

The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.bloch` section's `mo_metadata` member: the orbital set the binary members carry. Per-orbital energies and occupations are the binary members `energies` and `occupations`, not fields of this payload. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.3.1 (wavefunction.bloch — k-resolved Bloch orbitals, provisional).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spin` | yes | one of `"restricted"` \| `"unrestricted"` | `restricted`: one set of spatial orbitals shared by both spins (n_spin 1). `unrestricted`: separate alpha and beta sets (n_spin 2). |
| `n_spin` | yes | integer | Number of spin channels; equals axis 1 of mo_coefficients, energies and occupations. |
| `n_mo` | yes | integer | Number of MOs at each k-point and spin; equals axis 2 of mo_coefficients, energies and occupations. |
| `n_ao` | yes | integer | Number of AOs; equals axis 3 of mo_coefficients and the basis payload's n_ao. |
| `orbital_kind` |  | one of 10 values | What the orbitals are, with the values and meanings of the wavefunction.gto mo_metadata field of the same name; absent means `canonical`. |
| `complex` | yes | const `true` | Always true: mo_coefficients carries (real, imaginary) pairs in its last axis. |
| `k_point_convention` | yes | one of `"fractional"` | How the kpoints member states k: `fractional`, in fractional coordinates of the reciprocal lattice. The only value in v1. |
| `n_mo_per_k` |  | array of integer | Number of orbitals that are defined at each k-point, one entry per k-point, each at most n_mo, for a producer whose orbital count differs between k-points (canonical orthogonalisation that removes a different number of near-linear-dependent directions at each k). Orbitals n_mo_per_k[k] to n_mo - 1 at k-point k are padding, with zero coefficients and zero occupations, and consumers ignore them. Absent means n_mo at every k-point. |
| `fermi_energy` |  | [`ValueWithUnits`](#def-valuewithunits) | Fermi level of the calculation, on the absolute scale of `energies`. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional map from the role of a member of the section to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `energies` is `hartree`. |

Fixed units: `energies` = `hartree`.

<a id="def-bondorderspayload"></a>

### `BondOrdersPayload`

Used by: [`bond_orders`](#kind-bond-orders).

The JSON payload named by a `bond_orders` section's `bond_orders` member: computed bond orders per atom pair. Strict: no keys other than those listed, except extension keys beginning with `x_`, here and in every pair. See QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | yes | string | Bond-order definition. Lowercase names are recommended, e.g. 'mayer', 'wiberg' or 'nbo'. |
| `pairs` | yes | array of object |  |

<a id="def-bondspayload"></a>

### `BondsPayload`

Used by: [`bonds`](#kind-bonds), [`structure`](#kind-structure).

The JSON payload of a `bonds` section's `bonds` member and of a `structure` section's optional `bonds` member: explicit connectivity as atom pairs. Strict: no keys other than those listed, except extension keys beginning with `x_`, here and in every pair. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds) and § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pairs` | yes | array of object |  |

<a id="def-dielectricpropertiespayload"></a>

### `DielectricPropertiesPayload`

Used by: [`properties.dielectric`](#kind-properties-dielectric).

The JSON payload named by a `properties.dielectric` section's `properties` member: the dielectric tensors, Born effective charges and piezoelectric tensor of a periodic system. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. That static equals electronic plus ionic, and that there is one Born tensor per atom of the structure, are checked by validators, not this schema. See QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `electronic` | yes | array[3] of array[3] of number | The electronic (high-frequency, clamped-ion) dielectric tensor, relative permittivity, dimensionless, rows and columns x, y, z. |
| `ionic` |  | array[3] of array[3] of number | The ionic (lattice) contribution to the static dielectric tensor, dimensionless. |
| `static` |  | array[3] of array[3] of number | The static dielectric tensor, dimensionless: the sum of electronic and ionic, to which it must agree within 1e-6 when all three are present. |
| `born_charges` |  | array[1..] of array[3] of array[3] of number | The Born effective charge tensor of each atom, in elementary charges, one 3 x 3 matrix per atom in atom order. Entry (i, j) is the polarization along i per unit displacement of the atom along j. |
| `piezoelectric` |  | array[3] of array[6] of number | The piezoelectric stress tensor e_ia in C/m^2: the row is the polarization component x, y, z, the column the Voigt strain index in the order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy. |
| `units` |  | object | Declared units, field name to unit name (QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions)): the three dielectric tensors are dimensionless and `born_charges` is e. v1 fixes them, so a declaration only restates them. The piezoelectric tensor, in C/m^2, has no unit name and is fixed by QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |

Fixed units: `electronic` = `dimensionless`, `ionic` = `dimensionless`, `static` = `dimensionless`, `born_charges` = `e`.

<a id="def-dosmetapayload"></a>

### `DosMetaPayload`

Used by: [`dos.coop`](#kind-dos-coop), [`dos.cohp`](#kind-dos-cohp).

The JSON payload named by the `meta` member of a `dos.coop` or `dos.cohp` section: what the pair axis of `projections` and `integrated` means, plus broadening and Fermi level. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Typed-open: the fields below are typed and further keys are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` |  | string | The bonding analysis, conventionally 'coop' or 'cohp'. |
| `n_spin` |  | integer | Number of spin channels; with 2, `projections` and `integrated` carry a leading spin axis. |
| `fermi_energy_ev` |  | number | Absolute Fermi level in eV (`energies` are referenced to it at 0). |
| `smearing` |  | number | Broadening width in eV. |
| `smearing_type` |  | string | Broadening function, e.g. 'gaussian'. |
| `pairs` |  | array of array[2] of integer or object | The atom pairs, one per entry of the pair axis: [i, j], or an object {i, j, label?, symbol_i?, symbol_j?, distance_ang?} with 0-based atom indices and the distance in Å. |
| `pair_labels` |  | array of string | Display labels, one per entry of the pair axis. |
| `channels` |  | array of [`DosChannel`](#def-doschannel) | Channel objects, one per entry of the pair axis; a pair channel names its two atoms as i and j. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional map from a field name of this payload, or the role of a member of the section, to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `fermi_energy_ev` and `energies` are `ev`. |

Fixed units: `fermi_energy_ev` = `ev`, `energies` = `ev`.

<a id="def-elasticpropertiespayload"></a>

### `ElasticPropertiesPayload`

Used by: [`properties.elastic`](#kind-properties-elastic).

The JSON payload named by a `properties.elastic` section's `properties` member: the elastic constants of a periodic system in Voigt notation. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. The stiffness and compliance matrices must be symmetric, which validators check, not this schema. See QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stiffness` | yes | array[6] of array[6] of number | The stiffness matrix C in Voigt notation, rows and columns in the order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy, in GPa. Symmetric. |
| `compliance` |  | array[6] of array[6] of number | The compliance matrix S, the inverse of the stiffness matrix, in Voigt notation, in 1/GPa. Symmetric. |
| `bulk_modulus_gpa` |  | number | Bulk modulus in GPa, by the scheme `average` names. |
| `shear_modulus_gpa` |  | number | Shear modulus in GPa, by the scheme `average` names. |
| `youngs_modulus_gpa` |  | number | Young's modulus in GPa, by the scheme `average` names. |
| `poisson_ratio` |  | number | Poisson's ratio, dimensionless, by the scheme `average` names. |
| `average` |  | one of `"voigt"` \| `"reuss"` \| `"hill"` | The averaging scheme of the four isotropic moduli: 'voigt' (uniform strain), 'reuss' (uniform stress) or 'hill' (their arithmetic mean). Absent means the scheme is not stated. |
| `units` |  | object | Declared units, field name to unit name (QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions)): `stiffness` and the three moduli are gpa, `poisson_ratio` is dimensionless. v1 fixes them, so a declaration only restates them. The compliance, in 1/GPa, has no unit name and is fixed by QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |

Fixed units: `stiffness` = `gpa`, `bulk_modulus_gpa` = `gpa`, `shear_modulus_gpa` = `gpa`, `youngs_modulus_gpa` = `gpa`, `poisson_ratio` = `dimensionless`.

<a id="def-electricpropertiespayload"></a>

### `ElectricPropertiesPayload`

Used by: [`properties.electric`](#kind-properties-electric).

The JSON payload named by a `properties.electric` section's `properties` member: the electric multipole moments and polarizabilities of the system, each block in the fixed unit of the spec. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed, here and in every block. At least one of dipole, quadrupole, octupole, polarizability and hyperpolarizability is required. See QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin` |  | string or array[3] of number | Reference point of the multipole moments, as `dipole_moment.origin` of the manifest root: a conventional name ('center_of_mass', 'center_of_nuclear_charge', 'origin') or an explicit 3-vector in bohr. |
| `dipole` |  | object | The electric dipole moment, in debye. When the manifest root also carries a `dipole_moment` block, the two statements must agree within 1e-6 debye; see QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |
| `quadrupole` |  | object | The electric quadrupole moment, in debye-angstrom, in the Cartesian axes of the structure. `convention` names the moment the matrix holds and `traceless` says whether its trace is zero; see QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |
| `octupole` |  | object | The electric octupole moment, in debye-angstrom^2, in the Cartesian axes of the structure; see QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |
| `polarizability` |  | object | The electric dipole polarizability at one frequency, in atomic units; see QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |
| `hyperpolarizability` |  | object | The first electric dipole hyperpolarizability at one pair of frequencies, in atomic units; see QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |
| `units` |  | object | Declared units, field name to unit name (QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions)): `dipole` is debye and `origin`, when it is a vector, bohr. v1 fixes both, so a declaration only restates them. The other fields have units that the vocabulary does not name; they are fixed by QVF spec § 5.13 (Property kinds). |

Fixed units: `dipole` = `debye`, `origin` = `bohr`.

<a id="def-eosfitpayload"></a>

### `EosFitPayload`

Used by: [`equation_of_state`](#kind-equation-of-state).

The JSON payload named by an `equation_of_state` section's `fit` member: the fitted equation-of-state model and its parameters. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | yes | one of `"birch_murnaghan"` \| `"murnaghan"` \| `"vinet"` \| `"poirier_tarantola"` \| `"polynomial"` | The fitted E(V) form: third-order Birch-Murnaghan, Murnaghan, Vinet, third-order Poirier-Tarantola, or a polynomial in V from which V0, E0, B0 and B0_prime are derived. |
| `V0` |  | number | Equilibrium volume in Å³. |
| `E0` |  | number | Energy at V0 in eV. |
| `B0` |  | number | Bulk modulus at V0 in GPa. |
| `B0_prime` |  | number | Pressure derivative of the bulk modulus at V0, dimensionless. |
| `residual_rms` |  | number | Root-mean-square residual of the fit over the data points, in eV. |
| `n_points` |  | integer | Number of (volume, energy) points the fit used. |
| `pressures_gpa` |  | array of number | Pressure of the fitted model at each volume point, in GPa, parallel to `volumes`. |
| `energy_unit` |  | string | Informational restatement of the energy unit, eV; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |
| `volume_unit` |  | string | Informational restatement of the volume unit, Å³; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |
| `pressure_unit` |  | string | Informational restatement of the pressure unit, GPa; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

<a id="def-eprspectrumpayload"></a>

### `EprSpectrumPayload`

Used by: [`spectra.epr`](#kind-spectra-epr).

The JSON payload named by a `spectra.epr` section's `spectrum` member: the g-tensor, per-nucleus hyperfine (A) tensors and the zero-field-splitting (D) tensor. Permissive: the known fields are typed, every object stays open, and a later revision may tighten the definition. Units are fixed: g-values are dimensionless, hyperfine and zero-field-splitting parameters are in MHz. See QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `g_tensor` |  | object |  |
| `hyperfine` |  | array of object | Hyperfine couplings, one entry per magnetic nucleus. |
| `zero_field_splitting` |  | object |  |

<a id="def-excitedstatespayload"></a>

### `ExcitedStatesPayload`

Used by: [`excited_states`](#kind-excited-states).

The JSON payload named by an `excited_states` section's `states` member. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. `states` lists the states in ascending order of their unique `index`; `meta` describes the calculation. That the indices are unique and ascending, that `meta.n_states` equals the number of states, that the references resolve and that the contributions index existing orbitals is checked by validators, not by this schema. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `states` | yes | array of [`ExcitedState`](#def-excitedstate) | The excited states, in ascending order of `index`. |
| `meta` |  | [`ExcitedStatesMeta`](#def-excitedstatesmeta) | Description of the calculation an `ExcitedStatesPayload` comes from. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`. No field is required; see QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties). |

<a id="def-fermimeshpayload"></a>

### `FermiMeshPayload`

Used by: [`fermi_surface`](#kind-fermi-surface).

The JSON payload named by a `fermi_surface` section's `mesh` member: the k-point mesh that the first three axes of `energies` sample, and the cell it lives in. Grid point (i1, i2, i3) of a uniform mesh lies at fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates (i1/nk1 + shift[0], i2/nk2 + shift[1], i3/nk3 + shift[2]). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` |  | array[3] of integer | Mesh dimensions [nk1, nk2, nk3]; equal to the first three axes of `energies`. |
| `nk1` |  | integer | Mesh dimension along b1 as a separate key; equals shape[0] when both are present. |
| `nk2` |  | integer | Mesh dimension along b2; equals shape[1] when both are present. |
| `nk3` |  | integer | Mesh dimension along b3; equals shape[2] when both are present. |
| `shift` |  | any | Position of grid point (0, 0, 0) in fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates. Absent means a Γ-centred mesh. |
| `symmetry_expanded` |  | boolean | True when the producer filled the full mesh by applying symmetry operations to an irreducible set of computed k-points. |
| `kpoints` |  | array of array[3] of number | Explicit fractional coordinates of every grid point, for a mesh that is not uniform: entry (i1 * nk2 + i2) * nk3 + i3 is grid point (i1, i2, i3). When present it replaces the uniform-mesh formula. |
| `fermi_energy_ev` |  | number | Absolute Fermi level in eV; `energies` hold E(k) - E_F. |
| `n_spin` |  | integer | Number of spin channels of the underlying calculation. |
| `band_indices` |  | array of integer | 0-based index, in the producer's full band list, of each band along the last axis of `energies`. |
| `lattice_vectors` |  | array[3] of array[3] of number | Real-space cell as three row vectors in Å (the structure convention); the reciprocal lattice follows from it. |
| `reciprocal_lattice` |  | array[3] of array[3] of number | Reciprocal lattice vectors b1, b2, b3 as rows, in 1/Å, including the 2π factor (a_i · b_j = 2π δ_ij). |
| `units` |  | object | Optional map from a field name of this payload, or the role of a member of the section, to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `fermi_energy_ev` and `energies` are `ev` and `lattice_vectors` is `angstrom`. |

Fixed units: `fermi_energy_ev` = `ev`, `energies` = `ev`, `lattice_vectors` = `angstrom`.

<a id="def-forcesmetapayload"></a>

### `ForcesMetaPayload`

Used by: [`forces`](#kind-forces).

The JSON payload named by a `forces` section's `meta` member. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. No field is required. See QVF spec § 5.10 (forces — nuclear gradient and stress).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `structure_ref` |  | string | Id of the structure section whose atoms the gradient rows follow. A section-level structure_ref takes precedence when both are present. |
| `method` |  | string | Method of the energy that was differentiated, e.g. 'rks'. |
| `convention` |  | one of `"gradient"` | What the gradient member holds: 'gradient', the energy gradient dE/dR, is the only value in v1. Absent means 'gradient'. |
| `units` |  | [`DerivativeUnits`](#def-derivativeunits) | Declared units of an energy-derivative payload (forces, hessian): `energy` and `length` name the units the derivatives are taken in. v1 fixes them at hartree and bohr, so a declaration restates them and cannot name another unit; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

<a id="def-hessianmetapayload"></a>

### `HessianMetaPayload`

Used by: [`hessian`](#kind-hessian).

The JSON payload named by a `hessian` section's `meta` member. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. No field is required, but a mass-weighted matrix requires atom_masses_amu. See QVF spec § 5.11 (hessian — Cartesian second derivatives).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `structure_ref` |  | string | Id of the structure section whose atoms index the matrix. A section-level structure_ref takes precedence when both are present. |
| `mass_weighted` |  | boolean | True when element (i, j) of the matrix is divided by sqrt(m_a m_b) for the atoms a and b of i and j, with the masses of atom_masses_amu, which is then required. Absent means false. |
| `projected` |  | boolean | True when the rigid-body translations and, for a non-periodic system, rotations have been projected out of the matrix. Absent means false. |
| `atom_masses_amu` |  | array of number | Mass of each atom in unified atomic mass units, in atom order: one entry per atom, N in all. |
| `units` |  | [`DerivativeUnits`](#def-derivativeunits) | Declared units of an energy-derivative payload (forces, hessian): `energy` and `length` name the units the derivatives are taken in. v1 fixes them at hartree and bohr, so a declaration restates them and cannot name another unit; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

<a id="def-jobspecpayload"></a>

### `JobSpecPayload`

Used by: [`job.spec`](#kind-job-spec).

The JSON payload named by a `job.spec` section's `spec` member (conventionally `job_spec/spec.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The root is open for forward growth, but engine-specific keywords SHOULD live under `options`, keeping the typed top level portable across codes; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_type` | yes | one of `"molecular"` \| `"periodic"` | Which class of engine runs the job. Periodicity of the geometry itself is carried by the structure section's pbc/lattice_vectors; job_type selects the runner, it does not restate periodicity. |
| `method` |  | string | Method identifier (e.g. 'rhf', 'rks', 'ccsd(t)', 'gfn2'). Producer-neutral lowercase recommended. Absent means the engine's default. |
| `basis` |  | string or null or const `""` | Basis-set name (e.g. 'def2-svp'), or null: the method takes no basis set (a semiempirical or tight-binding method). Absent means the engine's default. The empty string is a deprecated spelling of null; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). |
| `functional` |  | string or null or const `""` | Exchange-correlation functional name (e.g. 'pbe0'), for DFT methods, or null: the method takes no functional (Hartree-Fock, a correlated wavefunction or a semiempirical method). Absent means the engine's default. The empty string is a deprecated spelling of null; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). |
| `charge` |  | integer | Net charge. Absent means 0. Authoritative for the job — never inferred from the structure. |
| `multiplicity` |  | integer | Spin multiplicity 2S+1. Absent means 1. |
| `kpoints` |  | array[3] of integer | [n1, n2, n3] Monkhorst-Pack mesh. Periodic jobs only. |
| `tasks` |  | array of string | Ordered task identifiers, e.g. ['single_point'], ['optimize', 'hessian']. Absent means a single point. |
| `structure_ref` |  | string | Id of the `structure` section the job runs on. A validator resolves it to a section of kind `structure`. A `structure_ref` on the `job.spec` section object takes precedence and is the preferred carrier, because it can be read from the manifest; producers keep the two equal. In an archive with several `structure` sections a job without either is ambiguous, and a runner refuses it; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification), under Job sets, and QVF spec § 4.1 (Section object). |
| `solvation` |  | [`JobSpecSolvation`](#def-jobspecsolvation) | Implicit solvation of a job: the `solvation` field of `JobSpecPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; engine-specific keywords go under `options`. |
| `dispersion` |  | string | Dispersion correction, by its conventional lowercase name, e.g. 'd3bj' or 'd4'. Absent means none beyond what the method implies. |
| `relativistic` |  | string | Scalar-relativistic treatment, by its conventional lowercase name, e.g. 'zora', 'x2c' or 'dkh2'. Absent means none. |
| `scf` |  | [`JobSpecScf`](#def-jobspecscf) | Self-consistent-field settings of a job: the `scf` field of `JobSpecPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; engine-specific keywords go under `options`. |
| `geometry` |  | [`JobSpecGeometry`](#def-jobspecgeometry) | Geometry-optimisation settings of a job: the `geometry` field of `JobSpecPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; engine-specific keywords go under `options`. |
| `resources` |  | [`JobSpecResources`](#def-jobspecresources) | Resources a job would like: the `resources` field of `JobSpecPayload`. These are hints, not requirements: a runner uses what it has and may use less. What a run actually used is recorded in `provenance` (`n_threads`, `n_mpi_ranks`, `n_gpus`, `wall_seconds`). See QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`. |
| `options` |  | object | Additional engine-specific keywords (JSON-safe values). A runner that does not recognize an option MUST refuse the job rather than silently drop it. |

<a id="def-kpathpayload"></a>

### `KpathPayload`

Used by: [`bands`](#kind-bands).

The JSON payload named by a `bands` section's `kpath` member: the path the eigenvalues are sampled on, the Fermi level, and the fat-band channels. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. No field is required. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kpoints` |  | array of array[3] of number | Fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates of every k-point along the path, in the order of eigenvalues axis 1 (n_kpoints entries). |
| `labels` |  | array of string | One label per k-point along the path, parallel to `kpoints` and eigenvalues axis 1; an empty string marks an unlabelled point. |
| `segments` |  | array of [`KpathSegment`](#def-kpathsegment) | The straight segments of the path, in path order. |
| `fermi` |  | number | Fermi level in eV, on the absolute scale of `eigenvalues` (eigenvalues are not shifted by it). |
| `fermi_energy_ev` |  | number | The Fermi level under the name the DOS kinds use. When both are present it equals `fermi`. |
| `spinor` |  | boolean | True when the bands come from a two-component (spin-orbit) calculation: n_spin is then 1 and each band is one spinor state. |
| `n_spin` |  | integer | Number of spin channels; equals eigenvalues axis 0. |
| `n_kpoints` |  | integer | Number of k-points along the path; equals eigenvalues axis 1. |
| `n_bands` |  | integer | Number of bands; equals eigenvalues axis 2. |
| `channels` |  | array of [`DosChannel`](#def-doschannel) or string | Fat-band channels, one per last-axis slice of `projections`. A string is shorthand for a channel object carrying only that `label`. |
| `title` |  | string | Display title of the band structure. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional map from a field name of this payload, or the role of a member of the section, to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `fermi`, `fermi_energy_ev` and `eigenvalues` are `ev`. |
| `kind` |  | const `"bands"` | Informational echo of the section kind. |
| `version` |  | string | Informational producer label for the payload layout; consumers do not rely on it. |
| `reciprocal_space` |  | boolean | Informational; k-points are always reciprocal-space coordinates. |

Fixed units: `fermi` = `ev`, `fermi_energy_ev` = `ev`, `eigenvalues` = `ev`.

<a id="def-mometadatapayload"></a>

### `MoMetadataPayload`

Used by: [`wavefunction.gto`](#kind-wavefunction-gto).

The JSON payload named by a `wavefunction.gto` section's `mo_metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/mo_metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. `spin` selects one of two shapes. `unrestricted` carries an `alpha` and a `beta` object, matching the `mo_coefficients_alpha` and `mo_coefficients_beta` members, and no top-level per-MO arrays. Every other `spin` value carries one set of orbitals, matching `mo_coefficients`, with `energies` and `occupations` at the top level and no `alpha` or `beta`. Per-MO arrays are in the row order of the coefficient member. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`. The deprecated keys `iao_charges`, `excitation_index` and `excitation_energy_ev` remain valid so that archives which carry them keep validating; producers write their canonical carriers instead; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
