| `spin` | yes | one of `"restricted"` \| `"unrestricted"` \| `"restricted_open"` \| `"generalized"` | `restricted`: one set of spatial orbitals shared by both spins. `unrestricted`: separate α and β sets. `restricted_open`: one set of spatial orbitals, singly or doubly occupied, in the restricted shape. `generalized`: one set of two-component spin orbitals that mix α and β, in the restricted shape with the AO axis of `mo_coefficients` doubled to 2 n_ao (the α components of the n_ao AOs, then their β components); it requires `complex: true`. See QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). |
| `orbital_kind` |  | one of 10 values | What the orbitals are; absent means `canonical`. `canonical`: eigenfunctions of the converged Fock or Kohn-Sham operator. `natural`: natural orbitals. `localized`: localized orbitals of an unnamed method. `nto`: natural transition orbitals. `nbo`: natural bond orbitals. `iao`, `ibo`: intrinsic atomic and bond orbitals. `boys`, `pipek_mezey`: Foster-Boys and Pipek-Mezey localized orbitals. `custom`: anything else. |
| `n_ao` |  | integer | Number of AOs; equals the `basis` payload's `n_ao`. |
| `n_mo` |  | integer | Number of MOs; equals the row count of `mo_coefficients`. |
| `energies` |  | array of number | Orbital energy of each MO, in Hartree. |
| `occupations` |  | array of number | Occupation of each MO: electrons per orbital, or a transition weight when `occupation_semantics` says so. |
| `symmetry_labels` |  | array of string | Irreducible-representation label of each MO, parallel to `energies`; validators check the length. |
| `alpha` |  | [`MoSpinChannel`](#def-mospinchannel) | The α orbitals of an unrestricted wavefunction; for NTOs they pair by row with the α channel of the other section, independently of β (QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto)). |
| `beta` |  | [`MoSpinChannel`](#def-mospinchannel) | The β orbitals of an unrestricted wavefunction; for NTOs they pair by row with the β channel of the other section, independently of α (QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto)). |
| `occupation_semantics` |  | one of `"electron_occupation"` \| `"transition_weight"` | Meaning of the `occupations` numbers: electrons per orbital (`electron_occupation`, the meaning when absent) or the weights of natural transition orbitals (`transition_weight`). |
| `k_point` |  | array[3] of number | Crystal momentum of the orbitals, in fractional coordinates of the reciprocal lattice; absent or [0, 0, 0] means the Γ point. |
| `complex` |  | boolean | true when every coefficient member is complex, float64 [n_mo, n_ao, 2] (2 n_ao for `generalized`) with the last axis (real, imaginary); absent or false means real [n_mo, n_ao]. Validators check the rank of the coefficient members against it. |
| `coefficient_encoding` |  | one of `"real"` \| `"complex_split_last_axis"` | Alternative spelling of `complex`: `real` means false, `complex_split_last_axis` means true. When both are present they MUST agree. |
| `coefficient_components` |  | array[2] of any | Order of the last axis of complex coefficients; when present it is ["real", "imag"]. |
| `state_ref` |  | string | Reference to the electronic state the orbitals describe, for state-specific orbitals. For natural transition orbitals (`orbital_kind` nto) it is the id of the `excited_states` section, and `state_index` names the state; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). |
| `state_index` |  | integer | The `index` of the state that the orbitals describe, in the `excited_states` section that `state_ref` names. |
| `nto_role` |  | one of `"hole"` \| `"particle"` | Which half of a state's natural transition orbitals the section holds: `hole`, the occupied-space orbitals, or `particle`, the virtual-space orbitals. Row k of the hole section pairs with row k of the particle section of the same state; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). |
| `localization_method` |  | string | Name of the method that localized the orbitals. |
| `localization_reference_basis` |  | string | Name of the minimal reference basis of free-atom AOs from which the intrinsic atomic orbitals were constructed, e.g. 'minao' (IAO and IBO localization; Knizia, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2013, 9, 4834). The IAOs, and the IAO charges and IBOs derived from them, depend on this choice; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). |
| `atom_populations` |  | array of array of number | [n_mo, n_atoms]: the fraction of each localized orbital on each atom; each row sums to 1. |
| `centroids_bohr` |  | array of array[3] of number | [n_mo, 3]: the centroid of each localized orbital, in bohr. |
| `n_centres` |  | array of integer | Number of atoms each localized orbital is centred on. |
| `iao_charges` |  | array of number | Deprecated; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). The IAO partial charge of each atom, in e. Producers SHOULD NOT write it: the canonical carrier is the `iao_charge` member of an `atom_properties` section. Kept so that archives which already carry it remain valid. |
| `excitation_index` |  | integer | Deprecated; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). The excited state that natural transition orbitals describe, by the producer's own numbering. Producers SHOULD NOT write it: the canonical carrier is `state_index`, the state's `index` in the `excited_states` section that `state_ref` names. Kept so that archives which already carry it remain valid. |
| `excitation_energy_ev` |  | number | Deprecated; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). The excitation energy, in eV, of the state that natural transition orbitals describe. Producers SHOULD NOT write it: the canonical carrier is the `excitation_energy` of the state that `state_index` names in the `excited_states` section that `state_ref` names. Kept so that archives which already carry it remain valid. |

<a id="def-nmrspectrumpayload"></a>

### `NmrSpectrumPayload`

Used by: [`spectra.nmr`](#kind-spectra-nmr).

The JSON payload named by a `spectra.nmr` section's `spectrum` member: per-nucleus chemical shifts, shielding tensors and spin-spin couplings rather than a frequency/intensity pair. Permissive: the known fields are typed, every object stays open, and a later revision may tighten the definition. Shifts and shieldings are in ppm, couplings in Hz. See QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isotope` |  | string | Observed nucleus, e.g. '1H' or '13C'. |
| `reference` |  | string | Shift reference, e.g. 'TMS'. |
| `solvent` |  | string | Solvent or solvation model, when one was used. |
| `chemical_shifts` |  | array of object | One entry per nucleus. |
| `shielding_tensors` |  | array of object | Full shielding tensors, one entry per nucleus. |
| `j_couplings` |  | array of object | Indirect spin-spin couplings, one entry per atom pair. |

<a id="def-phononmetapayload"></a>

### `PhononMetaPayload`

Used by: [`phonon_dos`](#kind-phonon-dos).

The JSON payload named by a `phonon_dos` section's `meta` member: counts, broadening, and the channels of a projected phonon DOS. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Typed-open: the fields below are typed and further keys are allowed; an empty object is valid. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_atoms` |  | integer | Number of atoms in the cell. |
| `n_modes` |  | integer | Number of phonon branches (3 n_atoms). |
| `smearing` |  | number | Broadening width in cm⁻¹. |
| `smearing_type` |  | string | Broadening function, e.g. 'gaussian'. |
| `channels` |  | array of [`DosChannel`](#def-doschannel) | Channels of a projected phonon DOS, one per projection row. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional map from a field name of this payload, or the role of a member of the section, to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `frequencies` is `cm-1`. |

Fixed units: `frequencies` = `cm-1`.

<a id="def-qpathpayload"></a>

### `QpathPayload`

Used by: [`phonon_bands`](#kind-phonon-bands).

The JSON payload named by a `phonon_bands` section's `qpath` member: the q-point path the frequencies are sampled on, laid out like a bands kpath. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. No field is required. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kpoints` |  | array of array[3] of number | Fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates of every q-point along the path, in the order of frequencies axis 0. |
| `labels` |  | array of string | One label per q-point along the path; an empty string marks an unlabelled point. |
| `segments` |  | array of [`KpathSegment`](#def-kpathsegment) | The straight segments of the path, in path order. |
| `n_kpoints` |  | integer | Number of q-points along the path; equals frequencies axis 0. |
| `n_atoms` |  | integer | Number of atoms in the cell. |
| `n_modes` |  | integer | Number of phonon branches (3 n_atoms); equals frequencies axis 1. |
| `has_eigenvectors` |  | boolean | Whether the section carries mode eigenvectors. |
| `channels` |  | array of [`DosChannel`](#def-doschannel) | Projection channels of atom-resolved phonon bands. |
| `title` |  | string | Display title of the phonon band structure. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional map from a field name of this payload, or the role of a member of the section, to the unit name of its values. The units are fixed by QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions); a declaration restates them and does not change them, so `frequencies` is `cm-1`. |

Fixed units: `frequencies` = `cm-1`.

<a id="def-qtaimpayload"></a>

### `QtaimPayload`

Used by: [`topology.qtaim`](#kind-topology-qtaim).

The JSON payload named by a `topology.qtaim` section's `critical_points` member: critical points of the electron density and the bond paths joining them. Permissive root with typed points: the known fields are typed, the root and each point stay open, and a later revision may tighten the definition. Every position (a point's `position`, a bond-path vertex) is Cartesian, in the unit `units.position` declares, and in Angstrom, the unit of the structure the points overlay, when that is absent. The default is provisional pending a maintainer decision, so producers SHOULD declare `units.position`; see QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | yes | array of object |  |
| `bond_paths` |  | array of object | Gradient paths of the density joining two nuclei through a bond critical point. |
| `units` |  | object | Unit names of the payload's numeric fields. `position` names the unit of every position; another key names the unit of the point field of the same name, for which v1 fixes no default; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

<a id="def-reactionpathmetadatapayload"></a>

### `ReactionPathMetadataPayload`

Used by: [`reaction.path`](#kind-reaction-path).

The JSON payload named by a `reaction.path` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. It carries every key of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, the keys it shares with a `trajectory` metadata payload, plus waypoint annotations, an optional reaction coordinate, and the keys that describe the optional per-frame volumes (the `frame_volumes` and `volume_grid` members). Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbols` |  | array of string | Element symbol of each atom. |
| `atomic_numbers` |  | array of integer | Atomic number of each atom. |
| `atoms` |  | array of [`TrajectoryAtom`](#def-trajectoryatom) | Atom identities as objects, an alternative to `symbols` and `atomic_numbers`. When more than one of the three is present they MUST describe the same atoms. |
| `n_frames` |  | integer | Number of frames; equals the leading dimension of `coords`. |
| `energies` |  | array of number | Energy of each frame, in Hartree. When the section also carries the binary `energies` member, the two MUST agree within 1e-10 hartree. |
| `kind` |  | one of `"optimization"` \| `"irc"` \| `"md"` \| `"neb"` \| `"scan"` \| `"custom"` | What produced the frames: a geometry optimization, an intrinsic reaction coordinate, molecular dynamics, a nudged elastic band, a coordinate scan (relaxed or rigid), or something else. |
| `pbc` |  | array[3] of boolean | Per-axis periodicity of the frames: axis i is periodic iff pbc[i], as in the `structure` payload. Absent means the frames are molecular. For a `trajectory` it is REQUIRED when the section carries a `lattice` member, and a true entry requires that member. |
| `ensemble` |  | one of `"nve"` \| `"nvt"` \| `"npt"` \| `"nph"` \| `"custom"` | Thermodynamic ensemble of a molecular-dynamics run: constant N, V, E; N, V, T; N, p, T; N, p, H; or another. |
| `timestep_fs` |  | number | Time between consecutive frames, in fs. When the section has no `times` member, frame k is at k * timestep_fs. |
| `precision` |  | one of `"float64"` \| `"float32"` | Floating-point precision of the `coords` member; absent means float64. It MUST agree with that member's dtype: float32 coords require "float32" here. |
| `units` |  | object | The `units` declaration of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, which also fixes the `lattice` member of a periodic path to `bohr` (columns, unlike the `lattice` of a trajectory); see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |
| `waypoints` |  | array of [`ReactionWaypoint`](#def-reactionwaypoint) | Annotated frames of the path. |
| `reaction_coordinate` |  | array of number | Value of the reaction coordinate at each frame, in frame order: the abscissa of an energy profile. |
| `reaction_coordinate_label` |  | string | Display label of the reaction coordinate. |
| `reaction_coordinate_unit` |  | string | Unit of `reaction_coordinate`, e.g. "bohr" or "rad". |
| `dim` |  | integer | Number of periodic dimensions, shared by every frame of a periodic path. |
| `dim_per_frame` |  | array of integer | Number of periodic dimensions of each frame, for a path whose frames differ; used instead of `dim`. |
| `volume_frame_index` |  | array of integer | For each slab of the `frame_volumes` member, in order, the 0-based path frame it belongs to, so that volumes can be emitted for a subset of the frames. One entry per slab. |
| `volume_label` |  | string | Display label of the per-frame volumes, e.g. "density". |
| `volume_isovalue` |  | number | Suggested isovalue for the per-frame volumes, in the unit of their data. |

Fixed units: `energies` = `hartree`, `coords` = `angstrom`, `times` = `fs`, `timestep_fs` = `fs`, `lattice` = `bohr`.

<a id="def-reactionschemepayload"></a>

### `ReactionSchemePayload`

Used by: [`reaction.scheme`](#kind-reaction-scheme).

The JSON payload named by a `reaction.scheme` section's `scheme` member (conventionally `<section id>/scheme.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it, and also checks that every participant names a `structure` section, that step ids are unique and that no structure occurs twice within one role of a step. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | yes | array[1..] of [`ReactionStep`](#def-reactionstep) | The steps of the scheme, in reading order. |

<a id="def-reactionwaypointspayload"></a>

### `ReactionWaypointsPayload`

Used by: [`reaction.waypoints`](#kind-reaction-waypoints).

The JSON payload named by a `reaction.waypoints` section's `waypoints` member (conventionally `<section id>/waypoints.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `waypoints` | yes | array of [`ReactionWaypoint`](#def-reactionwaypoint) | Annotated frames of the trajectory named by the section's `trajectory_ref`. |
| `reaction_coordinate` |  | array of number | Value of the reaction coordinate at each frame of that trajectory, in frame order. |

<a id="def-runrecordfilespayload"></a>

### `RunRecordFilesPayload`

Used by: [`run.record`](#kind-run-record).

The JSON payload named by a `run.record` section's `files` member: an index from member role to what the member was before it was embedded. Every key names a member of the same section (`input`, `log` or an `attachment.<suffix>`), so the index has no vendor escape at its top level; each entry is strict apart from keys beginning with x_. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against this definition. See QVF spec § 5.8 (run.record — self-contained run records).

<a id="def-scansurfacemetadatapayload"></a>

### `ScanSurfaceMetadataPayload`

Used by: [`scan.surface`](#kind-scan-surface).

The JSON payload named by a `scan.surface` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The structured axis descriptions `axis_a` and `axis_b` are preferred; the flat label keys are recognised alternatives, and when both forms are present the objects take precedence. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `axis_a` |  | [`ScanSurfaceAxis`](#def-scansurfaceaxis) | The first driven coordinate, along the rows of `energies`. |
| `axis_b` |  | [`ScanSurfaceAxis`](#def-scansurfaceaxis) | The second driven coordinate, along the columns of `energies`. |
| `axis_a_label` |  | string | Flat alternative to `axis_a.label`. |
| `axis_b_label` |  | string | Flat alternative to `axis_b.label`. |
| `coordinate_a_label` |  | string | Flat alternative to `axis_a.label`. |
| `coordinate_a_unit` |  | string | Flat alternative to `axis_a.unit`. |
| `coordinate_b_label` |  | string | Flat alternative to `axis_b.label`. |
| `coordinate_b_unit` |  | string | Flat alternative to `axis_b.unit`. |
| `atoms` |  | array of [`TrajectoryAtom`](#def-trajectoryatom) | Atom identities, in the atom order of the `geometries` member. |
| `energy_unit` |  | string | Unit of the `energies` member values; absent means Hartree. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional declaration of units: each key names a field of this payload or the role of a member of the section (`axis_a`, `axis_b`, `energies`, `geometries`), each value a unit name. A declared unit is the unit the values are stored in. When `units.energies` and `energy_unit`, or a `units` entry and an axis `unit`, are both present they MUST name the same unit; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

<a id="def-scfhistorypayload"></a>

### `ScfHistoryPayload`

Used by: [`scf_history`](#kind-scf-history).

The JSON payload named by a `scf_history` section's `iterations` member: one record per SCF iteration. Strict: no keys other than those listed, except extension keys beginning with `x_`, here and in every record. See QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iterations` | yes | array of object |  |
| `converged` |  | boolean | Whether the SCF met its convergence criteria. Absent means not stated. |

<a id="def-spectrumpayload"></a>

### `SpectrumPayload`

Used by: [`spectra.ir`](#kind-spectra-ir), [`spectra.raman`](#kind-spectra-raman), [`spectra.uvvis`](#kind-spectra-uvvis), [`spectra.ecd`](#kind-spectra-ecd), [`spectra.vcd`](#kind-spectra-vcd), [`spectra.generic`](#kind-spectra-generic).

The JSON payload named by the `spectrum` member of a one-dimensional spectrum section: `spectra.ir`, `spectra.raman`, `spectra.uvvis`, `spectra.ecd`, `spectra.vcd` or `spectra.generic`. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition; a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Typed-open: the fields below are typed and the root stays open. `frequencies` carries the x axis in the unit QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions) gives the kind, unless `x_units` declares another; the name is kept for every kind, including those whose x values are energies. `frequencies`, `intensities` and, when present, `x` MUST have the same length. JSON Schema cannot express that rule, so a validator checks it separately; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra) and § 6 (Validation semantics).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frequencies` | yes | array of number | The x value of every point or line. Unit: the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions), or `x_units` when present. |
| `intensities` | yes | array of number | The y value of each entry of `frequencies`, in the same order. Unit: the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions), or `y_units` when present. |
| `x` |  | array of number | Optional alias of `frequencies` under a quantity-neutral name: the same values in the same order. `frequencies` stays REQUIRED; a consumer may read either. |
| `x_units` |  | one of 25 values | Unit name of `frequencies` and `x`. Absent means the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |
| `y_units` |  | one of 25 values | Unit name of `intensities`. Absent means the kind's unit from QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |
| `peaks` |  | array of [`SpectrumPeak`](#def-spectrumpeak) | Annotated peaks, in the units of `frequencies` and `intensities`. |
| `broadening` |  | object | The line shape the producer applied to turn discrete lines into an envelope, or recommends a consumer to apply. |
| `temperature_k` |  | number | Temperature the spectrum refers to, in kelvin. |
| `raman` |  | object | Raman-specific data, meaningful in a `spectra.raman` payload. |
| `uvvis` |  | object | UV-Vis-specific data, meaningful in a `spectra.uvvis` payload. |
| `states_ref` |  | string | Id of the `excited_states` section whose states the peaks name: every `peaks[].assignment.state_index` is then the `index` of a state of that section. It must name a section of kind `excited_states` in this archive; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra). |

<a id="def-structurepayload"></a>

### `StructurePayload`

Used by: [`structure`](#kind-structure).

The JSON payload named by a `structure` section's `structure` member (conventionally `structure/structure.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. `pbc` is the normative carrier of per-axis periodicity; `dimensionality` is a derived convenience. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atoms` | yes | array of [`StructureAtom`](#def-structureatom) |  |
| `pbc` |  | array[3] of boolean | Per-axis periodicity: axis i is periodic iff pbc[i]. REQUIRED when `lattice_vectors` is a non-null array; absent means a molecule ([false, false, false]). All eight patterns are legal — the periodic axes need NOT be the leading ones. |
| `lattice_vectors` |  | array[3] of array[3] of number or null | REQUIRED (non-null) when any pbc[i] is true; null or absent for a molecule. For every axis i with pbc[i] false, row i is non-physical bookkeeping — producers keep the matrix full-rank 3x3 so integrals and symmetry finders always see a 3-D lattice. Such a row is not a cell edge: a consumer MUST NOT draw it, replicate along it, or read it as a vacuum extent. |
| `dimensionality` |  | integer | Derived count of periodic axes: equal to the number of true entries in `pbc`. Optional, and MUST agree when present. It carries no axis identity — a consumer MUST NOT infer WHICH axes are periodic from it. |

<a id="def-symmetrypayload"></a>

### `SymmetryPayload`

Used by: [`structure.symmetry`](#kind-structure-symmetry).

The JSON payload named by a `structure.symmetry` section's `data` member: a symmetry analysis of the structure, as common symmetry finders report it. Permissive: the known fields are typed, the root stays open, and a later revision may tighten the definition. See QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spacegroup_number` |  | integer | Space-group number of the International Tables for Crystallography. |
| `international` |  | string | Short international (Hermann-Mauguin) space-group symbol, e.g. 'Fm-3m'. |
| `hall` |  | string | Hall symbol of the space group. |
| `point_group` |  | string | Point-group symbol; Schoenflies notation is recommended, e.g. 'C2v'. |
| `hermann_mauguin` |  | string | The point group in Hermann-Mauguin notation, e.g. 'mm2'. |
| `space_group_number` |  | integer | The same quantity as `spacegroup_number`, under the name some producers write. When both are present they MUST agree. |
| `space_group_symbol` |  | string | The same quantity as `international`, under the name some producers write. When both are present they MUST agree. |
| `operations` |  | array of object | Symmetry operations x' = R x + t. For a periodic structure R and t act on fractional coordinates of the structure's lattice; for a molecule R acts on Cartesian coordinates and t is zero or absent. |
| `wyckoffs` |  | array of string | Wyckoff letter of each atom, in the order of the structure's atoms. |
| `equivalent_atoms` |  | array of integer | For each atom, the 0-based index of the representative atom of its symmetry-equivalence class. |
| `symprec` |  | number | Distance tolerance of the symmetry search, in Angstrom. |

<a id="def-trajectorymetadatapayload"></a>

### `TrajectoryMetadataPayload`

Used by: [`trajectory`](#kind-trajectory).

The JSON payload named by a `trajectory` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. It carries the keys of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, which a `reaction.path` metadata payload shares (ReactionPathMetadataPayload), and fixes the units of the members only a trajectory has. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbols` |  | array of string | Element symbol of each atom. |
| `atomic_numbers` |  | array of integer | Atomic number of each atom. |
| `atoms` |  | array of [`TrajectoryAtom`](#def-trajectoryatom) | Atom identities as objects, an alternative to `symbols` and `atomic_numbers`. When more than one of the three is present they MUST describe the same atoms. |
| `n_frames` |  | integer | Number of frames; equals the leading dimension of `coords`. |
| `energies` |  | array of number | Energy of each frame, in Hartree. When the section also carries the binary `energies` member, the two MUST agree within 1e-10 hartree. |
| `kind` |  | one of `"optimization"` \| `"irc"` \| `"md"` \| `"neb"` \| `"scan"` \| `"custom"` | What produced the frames: a geometry optimization, an intrinsic reaction coordinate, molecular dynamics, a nudged elastic band, a coordinate scan (relaxed or rigid), or something else. |
| `pbc` |  | array[3] of boolean | Per-axis periodicity of the frames: axis i is periodic iff pbc[i], as in the `structure` payload. Absent means the frames are molecular. For a `trajectory` it is REQUIRED when the section carries a `lattice` member, and a true entry requires that member. |
| `ensemble` |  | one of `"nve"` \| `"nvt"` \| `"npt"` \| `"nph"` \| `"custom"` | Thermodynamic ensemble of a molecular-dynamics run: constant N, V, E; N, V, T; N, p, T; N, p, H; or another. |
| `timestep_fs` |  | number | Time between consecutive frames, in fs. When the section has no `times` member, frame k is at k * timestep_fs. |
| `precision` |  | one of `"float64"` \| `"float32"` | Floating-point precision of the `coords` member; absent means float64. It MUST agree with that member's dtype: float32 coords require "float32" here. |
| `units` |  | object | The `units` declaration of TrajectoryMetadataCommon, which also fixes the trajectory-only members: `lattice` is `angstrom` (rows, the structure convention), `cell_volumes` is `a3` and `temperatures` is `kelvin`; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

Fixed units: `energies` = `hartree`, `coords` = `angstrom`, `times` = `fs`, `timestep_fs` = `fs`, `lattice` = `angstrom`, `cell_volumes` = `a3`, `temperatures` = `kelvin`.

<a id="def-vibrationsmetadatapayload"></a>

### `VibrationsMetadataPayload`

Used by: [`vibrations`](#kind-vibrations).

The JSON payload named by a `vibrations` section's `metadata` member (conventionally `<section id>/metadata.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Per-mode arrays hold one entry per mode, in the mode order of `displacements`. An imaginary mode is written as a negative frequency whose magnitude is the imaginary wavenumber. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frequencies` | yes | array of number | Harmonic wavenumber of each mode, in cm⁻¹; negative for an imaginary mode. |
| `ir_intensities` |  | array of number | IR intensity of each mode, in km·mol⁻¹. |
| `raman_activities` |  | array of number | Raman scattering activity of each mode, in Å⁴·amu⁻¹. |
| `reduced_masses` |  | array of number | Reduced mass of each mode, in amu. |
| `force_constants` |  | array of number | Force constant of each mode, in mdyn·Å⁻¹. |
| `symmetry_labels` |  | array of string | Irreducible-representation label of each mode. |
| `imaginary` |  | array of boolean | Per-mode flag, true for an imaginary mode. When present it MUST agree with the sign of `frequencies`. |
| `n_modes` |  | integer | Number of modes; equals the leading dimension of `displacements`. |
| `symbols` |  | array of string | Element symbol of each atom, in the atom order of `displacements`. |
| `atoms` |  | array of [`StructureAtom`](#def-structureatom) | The reference geometry: one atom per atom of `displacements`, in the same order, with Cartesian positions in Ångström. |

<a id="def-volumegridpayload"></a>

### `VolumeGridPayload`

Used by: [`volume.density`](#kind-volume-density), [`volume.orbital`](#kind-volume-orbital), [`volume.spin`](#kind-volume-spin), [`volume.elf`](#kind-volume-elf), [`volume.difference`](#kind-volume-difference), [`volume.generic`](#kind-volume-generic), [`volume.potential`](#kind-volume-potential), [`volume.rdg`](#kind-volume-rdg), [`basis.ao`](#kind-basis-ao), [`reaction.path`](#kind-reaction-path), [`volume.laplacian`](#kind-volume-laplacian), [`volume.vector`](#kind-volume-vector), [`volume.complex`](#kind-volume-complex), [`volume.series`](#kind-volume-series), [`volume.transition_density`](#kind-volume-transition-density).

The JSON payload named by the `grid` member of every volume.* section and of a `basis.ao` section, and by the `volume_grid` member of a `reaction.path` section (conventionally `volumes/<section id>_grid.json`). It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. The grid is point-centred: data index (i, j, k) lies at origin + i·v_i + j·v_j + k·v_k, so the data holds exactly `shape` points. Along an axis a that `periodic` marks, the grid samples one period of the cell of its structure: voxel_vectors[a] × (shape[a] − 1) spans lattice vector a when `includes_endpoint` is true (the default, cube style: the last plane repeats the first), and voxel_vectors[a] × shape[a] spans it when `includes_endpoint` is false (CHGCAR style); validators check the span. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin` | yes | array[3] of number | Cartesian position of grid point (0, 0, 0), in bohr. |
| `voxel_vectors` | yes | array[3] of array[3] of number | The step vectors v_i, v_j, v_k, in bohr: row n is the displacement between neighbouring points along data axis n. Non-zero off-diagonal components describe a non-orthogonal grid. |
| `shape` | yes | array[3] of integer | Number of points [nx, ny, nz] along the three spatial data axes. It equals the shape of the section's 3-D `data` member, the leading three dimensions of a `volume.vector` or `volume.complex` `data` member, or the trailing three dimensions of a `volume.series` `data` member or of a `reaction.path` section's `frame_volumes` member. |
| `periodic` |  | array[3] of boolean | Per-axis periodicity of the sampled field: periodic[a] true means the field repeats with lattice vector a of the grid's structure along data axis a, so a consumer may tile or wrap the grid along it. Absent means [false, false, false], a finite box. An axis may be periodic only where the structure's `pbc` is true, and voxel_vectors[a] must then span lattice vector a as `includes_endpoint` says; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*). |
| `includes_endpoint` |  | boolean | Whether the points along a periodic axis include the endpoint of the period. true (the default, cube-file style): the last plane is the image of the first, shape[a] − 1 steps span one period, and a consumer that tiles or wraps the grid MUST drop the duplicated plane. false (CHGCAR style): shape[a] distinct planes span one period, exclusive of the endpoint. It matters only on periodic axes; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*). |
| `structure_ref` |  | string | Id of the `structure` section whose cell the grid samples. It must name a section of kind `structure` in the archive. The section-level `structure_ref` takes precedence when both are present; with neither, the archive's only `structure` section is the grid's structure. See QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*). |
| `units` |  | object | Optional declaration of units: each key names a field of this payload or the role of a member of the section, each value a unit name. `origin` and `voxel_vectors` are fixed to `bohr`, and a declaration restates that; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

Fixed units: `origin` = `bohr`, `voxel_vectors` = `bohr`.

<a id="def-volumeseriesaxispayload"></a>

### `VolumeSeriesAxisPayload`

Used by: [`volume.series`](#kind-volume-series).

The JSON payload named by the `axis` member of a `volume.series` section (conventionally `volumes/<section id>_axis.json`): what indexes the leading axis of the section's `data` member, one entry per slab. It is an archive member, not part of manifest.json, so nothing in the manifest $refs this definition — a validator loads the member's bytes and checks them against it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.2 (volume.*).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | yes | one of `"time"` \| `"frame"` \| `"state"` \| `"custom"` | What indexes the slabs: `time` (the values are times), `frame` (0-based frame indices of the trajectory or reaction path named by `trajectory_ref`), `state` (electronic states, the values being state indices or energies) or `custom` (anything else, which `labels` describe). |
| `values` | yes | array of number | The axis value of each slab, in slab order. It has n entries, n being the leading extent of `data`, which validators check. |
| `units` |  | one of 25 values | Unit of `values`, a unit name. Absent means the values are pure numbers (`dimensionless`), as frame and state indices are; a time axis should declare its unit (`fs` or `ps`). |
| `labels` |  | array of string | Display label of each slab, n entries, e.g. "S1" for an excited state. |
| `trajectory_ref` |  | string | Id of the `trajectory` or `reaction.path` section whose frames the slabs belong to; the frame indices of a `frame` axis index its `coords`. It must name a section of one of those two kinds. |

## Other definitions

The object definitions the fields above refer to, in alphabetical order.

<a id="def-atompropertymetaentry"></a>

### `AtomPropertyMetaEntry`

The description of one `custom.<name>` role in the `meta` member of an `atom_properties` section. Strict: only the fields below and keys beginning with x_ are allowed. See QVF spec § 5.7 (Analysis kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `units` | yes | any | The unit of the role's values, spelled as in QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions) where that gives a spelling; `dimensionless` for a pure number. |
| `description` | yes | string | What the quantity is, including any sign convention. |
| `kind` | yes | one of `"scalar"` \| `"vector"` | `scalar` for a float64 [n_atoms] member, `vector` for a float64 [n_atoms, 3] member. |

<a id="def-basisecpcentre"></a>

### `BasisEcpCentre`

The effective core potential on one atom of a `basis` payload: it replaces the `n_core_electrons` innermost electrons of that atom, which the wavefunction therefore does not describe. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `center` | yes | integer | 0-based index of the atom, as for a shell's `center`. |
| `n_core_electrons` | yes | integer | Number of electrons the potential replaces on this atom: the wavefunction describes the remaining Z − n_core_electrons of the atom's electrons. |
| `label` |  | string | Name of the potential, e.g. "def2-ECP". |
| `projectors` |  | array of [`BasisEcpProjector`](#def-basisecpprojector) | The radial functions of the potential: at most one local part and the semi-local channels. Absent: the potential is named by `label` and its core count only, and a consumer that needs the potential itself cannot evaluate it. |

<a id="def-basisecpprojector"></a>

### `BasisEcpProjector`

One radial function of an effective core potential, in the conventional semi-local form U(r) = Σ_i c_i r^(n_i − 2) exp(−α_i r²), with r in bohr and U in hartree: parallel arrays with one entry per term i, which MUST have the same length (JSON Schema cannot express that rule, so this definition does not check it). With `local: true` it is the local part of the centre's potential, which acts on every angular momentum; otherwise it is the semi-local channel of angular momentum `l`, which acts through the projector onto `l`. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `l` | yes | integer | Angular momentum of the channel. For the local part (`local: true`) it is the conventional label L of that part, which is greater than the `l` of every semi-local channel of the centre. |
| `exponents` | yes | array[1..] of number | Gaussian exponents α_i of the terms, in bohr⁻². |
| `coefficients` | yes | array[1..] of number | Coefficients c_i of the terms, in hartree · bohr^(2 − n_i), so that every term is an energy in hartree. |
| `powers` | yes | array[1..] of integer | Radial powers n_i of the terms: term i is c_i r^(n_i − 2) exp(−α_i r²), so n_i = 2 is a plain Gaussian and n_i = 0 carries r^(−2). |
| `local` |  | boolean | true: this radial function is the local part U_L(r) of the centre's potential, which acts on every angular momentum; a centre has at most one, and its `l` is the highest on the centre. false or absent: a semi-local channel, which multiplies the projector onto angular momentum `l`. As in the usual tabulations, a semi-local channel of a centre with a local part holds the difference U_l(r) − U_L(r). |

<a id="def-basisshell"></a>

### `BasisShell`

One contracted shell of a `basis` payload. It contributes 2l+1 (spherical) or (l+1)(l+2)/2 (Cartesian) AOs, ordered as in QVF spec Appendix A.2. `exponents` and `coefficients` are parallel, one entry per primitive, and MUST have the same length; JSON Schema cannot express that rule, so this definition does not check it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `center` | yes | integer | 0-based index of the atom the shell sits on, in the `atoms` of the `structure` section named by the payload's `structure_ref`. |
| `l` | yes | integer | Angular momentum of the shell (0 = s, 1 = p, 2 = d, …). |
| `exponents` | yes | array[1..] of number | Primitive exponents, in bohr⁻². |
| `coefficients` | yes | array[1..] of number | Contraction coefficients, one per exponent, applying to primitives normalized as QVF spec Appendix A.1 prescribes. |
| `pure` |  | boolean | true = spherical harmonics, false = Cartesian. Overrides the payload-level `pure` for this shell. |

<a id="def-biomoleculeresidue"></a>

### `BiomoleculeResidue`

One residue of a biomolecular `structure` section. `atom_indices` are 0-based indices into the `structure` member payload's `atoms` array. Residues are listed in chain order — the order a consumer draws a ribbon in — not sorted by `seq`, because insertion codes and non-monotonic numbering are both legal and sorting would silently reorder them. See QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | string | Residue name, e.g. "GLY". |
| `seq` | yes | integer | Residue sequence number (PDB cols 23-26). Not unique across a solvated system: PDB numbering is four columns wide and wraps at 9999, so a consumer MUST NOT use it as a global key. |
| `chain` | yes | string | Chain id this residue belongs to; matches an entry of the section's `chains` when that is present. |
| `insertion_code` |  | string | Residue insertion code (PDB col 27), e.g. "A" for residue 10A; absent means none. With `chain` and `seq` it identifies the residue: residues 10 and 10A of one chain are two entries, never merged. When the residue's atoms carry a per-atom `insertion_code` they MUST agree with it. |
| `atom_indices` | yes | array of integer | 0-based indices into the structure payload's `atoms` array. |

<a id="def-biomoleculesecondarystructure"></a>

### `BiomoleculeSecondaryStructure`

One inclusive secondary-structure range on one chain. A producer knows things a consumer cannot infer from CA geometry alone (alpha vs pi vs 3-10 helix, beta bridge vs sheet), so a consumer that also has its own geometric assignment MUST prefer these ranges where they are supplied; see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | yes | one of `"helix"` \| `"sheet"` \| `"coil"` |  |
| `chain` | yes | string |  |
| `start_seq` | yes | integer | First residue `seq` of the range, inclusive. |
| `end_seq` | yes | integer | Last residue `seq` of the range, inclusive. |

<a id="def-citationsreferences"></a>

### `CitationsReferences`

BibTeX bytes are carried as a binary member; consumers decode as UTF-8.

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | yes | string | Path of the member inside the zip archive. Forward slashes; no leading slash; no '..' segments. |
| `format` | yes | const `"binary"` |  |
| `sha256` | yes | string |  |
| `size` |  | integer | Uncompressed byte count of the stored member: it must equal the uncompressed size the ZIP central directory records for the member's entry, which a validator checks before reading the member. Optional on every member spec. See QVF spec § 4.2 (Member specs). |
| `media_type` |  | string | IANA media type of the member's bytes, a type and a subtype without parameters (RFC 6838), e.g. 'image/png' or 'text/plain'. Optional on every member spec; it describes the bytes and changes nothing in how they are read. A kind may require it, as `preview` does. See QVF spec § 4.2 (Member specs). |

<a id="def-derivativeunits"></a>

### `DerivativeUnits`

Declared units of an energy-derivative payload (forces, hessian): `energy` and `length` name the units the derivatives are taken in. v1 fixes them at hartree and bohr, so a declaration restates them and cannot name another unit; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `energy` |  | const `"hartree"` | Energy unit of the derivatives: hartree. |
| `length` |  | const `"bohr"` | Length unit of the derivatives: bohr. |

<a id="def-doschannel"></a>

### `DosChannel`

One projection channel of a DOS, fat-band or phonon projection: the atom, shell and component a slice of the projections belongs to. Typed-open: the fields below are typed and further keys are allowed. An absent field means the channel sums over that quantity (no `atom`: all atoms; no `l`: all shells; no `m`: all components of the shell). See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atom` |  | integer | 0-based index of the atom in the structure section. |
| `l` |  | integer | Angular momentum of the shell (0 = s, 1 = p, ...). |
| `m` |  | integer | Component within a spherical shell, -l..l, as in QVF spec Appendix A.2. |
| `spin` |  | integer | 0 (alpha) or 1 (beta) for a channel that is itself spin-resolved, which arises only in projections without a spin axis. |
| `label` | yes | string | Display label, e.g. 'Fe-3d'. |

<a id="def-excitedstate"></a>

### `ExcitedState`

One excited state of an `ExcitedStatesPayload`. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | yes | integer | Number of the state, unique within the payload and counted from 1; the reference state is not listed. Spectrum peaks (`assignment.state_index`), natural transition orbitals (`mo_metadata.state_index`) and transition densities (`state_index`) name a state by this number. |
| `excitation_energy` | yes | [`ValueWithUnits`](#def-valuewithunits) | Vertical excitation energy: the energy of the state minus the energy of the reference state. Producers SHOULD write it in `ev`. |
| `total_energy` |  | [`ValueWithUnits`](#def-valuewithunits) | Total energy of the state. Producers SHOULD write it in `hartree`. |
| `multiplicity` |  | integer | Spin multiplicity 2S + 1 of the state. |
| `symmetry` |  | string | Irreducible-representation label of the state, e.g. 'B1'. |
| `oscillator_strength` |  | number | Oscillator strength of the transition from the reference state, dimensionless. |
| `rotatory_strength_cgs` |  | number | Rotatory strength of the transition from the reference state, signed, in units of 10^-40 esu^2 cm^2 (the '10^-40 cgs' unit quantum-chemistry programs print). |
| `transition_dipole` |  | array[3] of number | Electric transition dipole moment between the reference state and the state, Cartesian components in atomic units (e bohr) in the axes of the section's structure. Its overall sign is arbitrary. |
| `transition_magnetic_dipole` |  | array[3] of number | Magnetic transition dipole moment between the reference state and the state, Cartesian components in atomic units (e hbar / m_e, twice the Bohr magneton) in the axes of the section's structure. |
| `contributions` |  | array of [`ExcitedStateContribution`](#def-excitedstatecontribution) | The dominant orbital excitations of the state. |
| `nto_ref` |  | string | Id of the `wavefunction.gto` section that holds the natural transition orbitals of the state: its hole orbitals, since the hole and particle orbitals are two sections; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). It must name a section of kind `wavefunction.gto`. |
| `density_ref` |  | string | Id of the section that holds a density of the state on a grid: a `volume.transition_density` section, or a `volume.difference` section holding the density of the state minus that of the reference state. |

<a id="def-excitedstatecontribution"></a>

### `ExcitedStateContribution`

One orbital excitation of an excited state: from orbital `from_mo` to orbital `to_mo` of the reference wavefunction. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from_mo` | yes | integer | 0-based row of the orbital the electron leaves, in the coefficient member of the reference wavefunction. |
| `to_mo` | yes | integer | 0-based row of the orbital the electron enters, in the coefficient member of the reference wavefunction. |
| `spin` |  | one of `"alpha"` \| `"beta"` | Spin channel of the excitation in an unrestricted reference: `alpha` indexes `mo_coefficients_alpha`, `beta` indexes `mo_coefficients_beta`. Absent for a reference with one set of orbitals. |
| `weight` | yes | number | Weight of the excitation in the state: the squared amplitude X^2 (CIS, TDA), or X^2 - Y^2 (full TD-DFT, RPA), normalized so that the weights of all excitations of a state sum to 1. |

<a id="def-excitedstatesmeta"></a>

### `ExcitedStatesMeta`

Description of the calculation an `ExcitedStatesPayload` comes from. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`. No field is required; see QVF spec § 5.12 (excited_states — excited states and transition properties).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` |  | string | Excited-state method, e.g. 'tddft', 'cis', 'adc2' or 'eom-ccsd'. |
| `reference_state` |  | string | The state the excitations start from, e.g. 'S0'. |
| `n_states` |  | integer | Number of states; equals the length of `states`. |
| `tda` |  | boolean | True when the Tamm-Dancoff approximation was used. |
| `spin_flip` |  | boolean | True when the states come from a spin-flip calculation. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional declaration of units, keyed by a field of the state objects, each value a unit name. `excitation_energy` and `total_energy` carry their unit in their own {value, units} objects, and a declaration restates it for every state; `oscillator_strength` is dimensionless. The transition dipoles and `rotatory_strength_cgs` have fixed units that no unit name names, so they are not declared; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

Fixed units: `oscillator_strength` = `dimensionless`.

<a id="def-jobspecgeometry"></a>

### `JobSpecGeometry`

Geometry-optimisation settings of a job: the `geometry` field of `JobSpecPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; engine-specific keywords go under `options`.

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `convergence` |  | number | Convergence threshold of the optimisation: the largest Cartesian gradient component, in hartree/bohr. |
| `max_steps` |  | integer | Maximum number of optimisation steps. |
| `coordinates` |  | one of `"cartesian"` \| `"internal"` \| `"redundant"` | Coordinate system the optimiser steps in. |

<a id="def-jobspecresources"></a>

### `JobSpecResources`

Resources a job would like: the `resources` field of `JobSpecPayload`. These are hints, not requirements: a runner uses what it has and may use less. What a run actually used is recorded in `provenance` (`n_threads`, `n_mpi_ranks`, `n_gpus`, `wall_seconds`). See QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`.

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_cores` |  | integer | Number of CPU cores to use. |
| `memory_mb` |  | integer | Memory to use, in megabytes. |
| `walltime_s` |  | number | Wall-clock time to allow, in seconds. |

<a id="def-jobspecscf"></a>

### `JobSpecScf`

Self-consistent-field settings of a job: the `scf` field of `JobSpecPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; engine-specific keywords go under `options`.

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `convergence` |  | number | Convergence threshold of the SCF energy change, in hartree. |
| `max_iterations` |  | integer | Maximum number of SCF iterations. |
| `guess` |  | string | Initial guess, by its conventional lowercase name, e.g. 'core', 'sad' or 'huckel'. |
| `damping` |  | number | Damping factor applied to the density or Fock update, dimensionless. |

<a id="def-jobspecsolvation"></a>

### `JobSpecSolvation`

Implicit solvation of a job: the `solvation` field of `JobSpecPayload`; see QVF spec § 5.9 (job.spec — declarative job specification). Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; engine-specific keywords go under `options`.

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | yes | string | Solvation model, by its conventional lowercase name, e.g. 'pcm', 'cpcm', 'smd' or 'cosmo'. |
| `solvent` |  | string | Solvent, by name, e.g. 'water'. |
| `epsilon` |  | number | Static dielectric constant of the solvent, dimensionless. |

<a id="def-kpathsegment"></a>

### `KpathSegment`

One straight segment of a band-structure path, listed in path order. Indices count points along the path axis (axis 1 of bands `eigenvalues`, axis 0 of phonon `frequencies`) from 0. When `start` is absent it is the previous segment's `end` (0 for the first segment), so consecutive segments share their boundary point; when `end` is absent it is start + n_points - 1. A path with a jump gives the segment after the jump an explicit `start`. Keys beginning with x_ are a vendor escape. See QVF spec § 5.6 (Bands, DOS, and periodic kinds).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` |  | integer | Index of the segment's first point. |
| `end` |  | integer | Index of the segment's last point (inclusive). |
| `n_points` |  | integer | Number of points on the segment, both ends included. |
| `label_start` |  | string | High-symmetry label of the first point (e.g. 'G' or 'Γ'); may be empty. |
| `label_end` |  | string | High-symmetry label of the last point; may be empty. |
| `k_start` |  | array[3] of number | Fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates of the first point. |
| `k_end` |  | array[3] of number | Fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates of the last point. |

<a id="def-mospinchannel"></a>

### `MoSpinChannel`

The orbitals of one spin channel of an unrestricted `mo_metadata` payload: per-MO arrays in the row order of the matching `mo_coefficients_alpha` or `mo_coefficients_beta` member. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_mo` |  | integer | Number of MOs in the channel; equals the row count of its coefficient member. |
| `energies` | yes | array of number | Orbital energy of each MO, in Hartree. |
| `occupations` | yes | array of number | Occupation of each MO, in electrons (0 to 1 in a spin channel), or a squared singular-value transition weight when occupation_semantics is transition_weight. For unrestricted NTOs, the nonnegative weights are in non-increasing order, match the paired section per spin, and both spins together sum to 1 for a normalized state; see QVF spec § 5.3 (wavefunction.gto). |
| `symmetry_labels` |  | array of string | Irreducible-representation label of each MO of the channel, parallel to its `energies`; validators check the length. |

<a id="def-previewimage"></a>

### `PreviewImage`

A larger or vector rendering of a `preview` section's picture: SVG, PNG or JPEG bytes as an opaque binary member. An SVG document is UTF-8, references no external resource and contains no script; see QVF spec § 5.15 (preview — a picture of the archive).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | yes | string | Path of the member inside the zip archive. Forward slashes; no leading slash; no '..' segments. |
| `format` | yes | const `"binary"` |  |
| `sha256` | yes | string |  |
| `size` |  | integer | Uncompressed byte count of the stored member: it must equal the uncompressed size the ZIP central directory records for the member's entry, which a validator checks before reading the member. Optional on every member spec. See QVF spec § 4.2 (Member specs). |
| `media_type` | yes | one of `"image/svg+xml"` \| `"image/png"` \| `"image/jpeg"` |  |

<a id="def-previewthumbnail"></a>

### `PreviewThumbnail`

The raster picture of a `preview` section: PNG or JPEG bytes as an opaque binary member. Its longest side SHOULD be 256 to 1024 pixels and the member SHOULD be at most 1 MiB; see QVF spec § 5.15 (preview — a picture of the archive).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | yes | string | Path of the member inside the zip archive. Forward slashes; no leading slash; no '..' segments. |
| `format` | yes | const `"binary"` |  |
| `sha256` | yes | string |  |
| `size` |  | integer | Uncompressed byte count of the stored member: it must equal the uncompressed size the ZIP central directory records for the member's entry, which a validator checks before reading the member. Optional on every member spec. See QVF spec § 4.2 (Member specs). |
| `media_type` | yes | one of `"image/png"` \| `"image/jpeg"` |  |

<a id="def-reactionenergydelta"></a>

### `ReactionEnergyDelta`

One reaction energy of a step, in hartree, with its optional conversion to kcal/mol. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value_eh` | yes | number | The reaction energy in hartree: the sum over the terms of coefficient times absolute value, within 1e-8 hartree. |
| `kcal_mol` |  | number | The same reaction energy in kcal/mol, `value_eh` × 627.509474 (CODATA 2018), within 1e-6 relative. |

<a id="def-reactionenergymethod"></a>

### `ReactionEnergyMethod`

The program and complete method specification of the run behind a term. Every term of one step has the same method; resource settings (cores, memory, wall time) do not belong in it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program` | yes | string | Program that computed the values, e.g. 'ORCA' or 'vibe-qc'. |
| `program_version` | yes | string | Version of that program, as it reports it. |
| `specification` | yes | object | The complete method of the run: task, method or functional, basis, dispersion, solvation, thermochemistry settings and every other option that changes the numbers, for example in the shape of a `job.spec` payload without its resources. Open. |

<a id="def-reactionenergysource"></a>

### `ReactionEnergySource`

The output file a term's absolute values were parsed from. The file itself is kept outside the archive, or in a `run.record` named by the term's `run_ref`. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | string | Basename of the output file, without a directory. |
| `sha256` | yes | string | SHA-256 of the output file's bytes, lowercase hex. |
| `parser` | yes | string | Name and version of the parser that read the values, e.g. 'orca-text/1'. |
| `input_sha256` |  | string | The producer's SHA-256 digest of the input species and geometry of the run, so a stale value is detectable; opaque to other consumers. |
| `locations` |  | object | Where each absolute value stands in the output file: a line number or key, keyed by the term field it fills. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`. |

<a id="def-reactionenergyterm"></a>

### `ReactionEnergyTerm`

One participant's contribution to a step's reaction energies: its structure, signed coefficient, absolute values in hartree, the method that produced them and where they came from. A term names its source run with `run_ref` (a `run.record` section of this archive), `source` (a file kept outside the archive), or both. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `structure_ref` | yes | string | Id of the `structure` section of the participant; it is a reactant or product of the step. |
| `coefficient` | yes | number | Signed stoichiometric coefficient: minus the participant's coefficient for a reactant, plus it for a product (a participant without a coefficient has 1). |
| `energy_eh` |  | number | Absolute energy of the participant, in hartree. REQUIRED when the step's `deltas` carries `energy`. |
| `enthalpy_eh` |  | number | Absolute enthalpy of the participant at the step's temperature and pressure, in hartree. REQUIRED when `deltas` carries `enthalpy`. |
| `gibbs_free_energy_eh` |  | number | Absolute Gibbs free energy of the participant at the step's temperature and pressure, in hartree. REQUIRED when `deltas` carries `gibbs_free_energy`. |
| `method` | yes | [`ReactionEnergyMethod`](#def-reactionenergymethod) | The program and complete method specification of the run behind a term. Every term of one step has the same method; resource settings (cores, memory, wall time) do not belong in it. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes). |
| `run_ref` |  | string | Id of the `run.record` section of this archive whose results the absolute values are. |
| `job_id` |  | string | The producer's identifier of the job that computed the values. |
| `run_id` |  | string | The producer's identifier of the run (one submission of that job). |
| `source` |  | [`ReactionEnergySource`](#def-reactionenergysource) | The output file a term's absolute values were parsed from. The file itself is kept outside the archive, or in a `run.record` named by the term's `run_ref`. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes). |

<a id="def-reactionparticipant"></a>

### `ReactionParticipant`

A species of a reaction step: the `structure` section that holds it and its stoichiometric coefficient. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `structure_ref` | yes | string | Id of the `structure` section of the species. It must name a section of kind `structure` in this archive. |
| `coefficient` |  | number | Stoichiometric coefficient of the species in the step; absent means 1. |

<a id="def-reactionstep"></a>

### `ReactionStep`

One step of a reaction scheme. Roles are chemical: `reactants` are consumed and `products` formed in the step's forward direction whatever the `arrow`, so for a retrosynthetic arrow the target is among the `products`. `energies` carries the step's reaction energies with the evidence they were computed from. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | string | Identifier of the step, unique within the payload. |
| `label` |  | string | Display label of the step, e.g. 'a' or 'step 2'. |
| `reactants` | yes | array[1..] of [`ReactionParticipant`](#def-reactionparticipant) | The species the step consumes. |
| `products` | yes | array[1..] of [`ReactionParticipant`](#def-reactionparticipant) | The species the step forms. |
| `reagents` |  | array of [`ReactionParticipant`](#def-reactionparticipant) | Species drawn at the arrow: reagents, catalysts, solvents drawn as structures. |
| `arrow` |  | one of `"forward"` \| `"equilibrium"` \| `"retrosynthetic"` \| `"resonance"` | The kind of arrow: 'forward' (reactants → products), 'equilibrium' (⇌), 'retrosynthetic' (products ⇒ reactants: target at the tail, precursors at the head) or 'resonance' (two resonance structures of one species, no reaction). Absent means 'forward'. |
| `conditions` |  | array of string | The text written at the arrow, one entry per line, in reading order. |
| `yield_percent` |  | number | Yield of the step's products, in percent. |
| `yield_text` |  | string | The yield as printed, e.g. '87%', '>95%' or 'quant.'. |
| `energies` |  | [`ReactionStepEnergies`](#def-reactionstepenergies) | Reaction energies of one `reaction.scheme` step: products minus reactants in the step's chemical forward direction, each delta the coefficient-weighted sum of the absolute energies of its `terms`. Every term names one participant with its signed coefficient, the run that produced its absolute values and the method of that run; all terms share one method and, for enthalpy and Gibbs free energy, one temperature and pressure. The numbers are a producer's parsed evidence, not a validation of minima or transition states. `version` 1 is this shape. A validator also checks that the terms match the step's participants, that the deltas equal the sums of the terms, that the kcal/mol values agree with the hartree values, that the methods agree and that every `run_ref` names a `run.record` section. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes). |

<a id="def-reactionstepenergies"></a>

### `ReactionStepEnergies`

Reaction energies of one `reaction.scheme` step: products minus reactants in the step's chemical forward direction, each delta the coefficient-weighted sum of the absolute energies of its `terms`. Every term names one participant with its signed coefficient, the run that produced its absolute values and the method of that run; all terms share one method and, for enthalpy and Gibbs free energy, one temperature and pressure. The numbers are a producer's parsed evidence, not a validation of minima or transition states. `version` 1 is this shape. A validator also checks that the terms match the step's participants, that the deltas equal the sums of the terms, that the kcal/mol values agree with the hartree values, that the methods agree and that every `run_ref` names a `run.record` section. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.14 (reaction.scheme — reaction schemes).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | yes | const `1` | Version of this payload shape. An additive revision keeps 1; an incompatible one takes a new value under a governance decision, and a consumer ignores an `energies` object of a version it does not know. |
| `deltas` | yes | object | The reaction energies of the step, at least one, keyed by quantity: `energy` (electronic or total energy), `enthalpy` and `gibbs_free_energy`. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`. |
| `temperature_k` |  | number | Temperature of the thermochemistry, in kelvin. REQUIRED when `deltas` carries `enthalpy` or `gibbs_free_energy`; one value for every term. |
| `pressure_atm` |  | number | Pressure of the thermochemistry, in atm. REQUIRED when `deltas` carries `enthalpy` or `gibbs_free_energy`; one value for every term. |
| `terms` | yes | array[2..] of [`ReactionEnergyTerm`](#def-reactionenergyterm) | One term per participant of the step that the reaction energy sums over: every reactant and product, and no reagent. |

<a id="def-reactionwaypoint"></a>

### `ReactionWaypoint`

One annotated frame of a reaction path, an item of the `waypoints` list of a `reaction.path` metadata payload or of a `reaction.waypoints` payload. Strict: any other key is an error unless it begins with `x_`; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame_index` | yes | integer | 0-based index of the annotated frame: into the section's own `coords` for `reaction.path`, into the `coords` of the trajectory named by `trajectory_ref` for `reaction.waypoints`. |
| `label` | yes | string | Display label, e.g. "TS1". |
| `kind` | yes | one of `"reactant"` \| `"transition_state"` \| `"intermediate"` \| `"product"` \| `"point"` | Role of the frame on the path; `point` marks any other annotated frame. |
| `energy_eh` |  | number | Energy of the frame, in Hartree. |

<a id="def-scansurfaceaxis"></a>

### `ScanSurfaceAxis`

One driven coordinate of a `scan.surface` section; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | yes | string | Display label of the coordinate. |
| `unit` |  | string | Unit of the coordinate values in the matching `axis_a` / `axis_b` binary member, e.g. "bohr" or "rad". |
| `atoms` |  | array of integer | 0-based indices of the atoms that define the coordinate: two for a distance, three for an angle, four for a dihedral. |

<a id="def-sectionvendor"></a>

### `SectionVendor`

Vendor-namespace section. The `kind` must start with `x_<vendor>`; member shape is unconstrained except that every member is a valid JsonMember, BinaryMember or OpaqueBinaryMember (binary bytes without dtype and shape, which SHOULD carry their `media_type`); see QVF spec § 7.3 (Vendor namespace x_<vendor>.*).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` |  | string |  |
| `members` |  | object |  |

<a id="def-spectrumpeak"></a>

### `SpectrumPeak`

One annotated peak of a `SpectrumPayload`. `x` and `width` are in the unit of the payload's `frequencies`, `y` in the unit of its `intensities`; see QVF spec § 5.4 (Spectra).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | yes | number | Peak position. |
| `y` |  | number | Peak intensity. |
| `width` |  | number | Full width at half maximum of the peak. |
| `label` |  | string |  |
| `assignment` |  | object | What the peak arises from. `mode_index` is a 0-based index into the modes of the archive's `vibrations` section; `state_index` identifies the electronic state the transition reaches: the `index` of a state of the `excited_states` section that the payload's `states_ref` names, or, without `states_ref`, as the producer numbers its states. |

<a id="def-structureatom"></a>

### `StructureAtom`

One atom of a `structure` payload. `position` is Cartesian, in Ångström — real coordinates, never fractional. Producers may add further per-atom fields; consumers ignore what they don't understand. Biomolecular producers conventionally add `atom_name` (PDB cols 13-16, e.g. "CA"), `residue_name` (cols 18-20), `residue_seq` (cols 23-26), `chain_id` (col 22) and `b_factor` (cols 61-66); of these only `b_factor` is typed here, because the other four predate this schema and archives in the wild carry `residue_seq` both as an integer and as a string. The optional typed `insertion_code`, `alt_loc`, `occupancy` and `hetero` complete the PDB/mmCIF atom-site identity: a residue is identified within its structure by (`chain_id`, `residue_seq`, `insertion_code`), and atoms of one residue that share `atom_name` but differ in `alt_loc` are alternate locations of one site; see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds), *Biomolecular atom identity*.

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | yes | string |  |
| `position` | yes | array[3] of number |  |
| `atomic_number` | yes | integer |  |
| `b_factor` |  | number | Per-atom temperature factor / pLDDT-style confidence (PDB cols 61-66). The per-atom carrier is authoritative over the section-level `b_factors` array, because it cannot desynchronize from its own atom; see QVF spec § 5.1 (structure and bonds). |
| `insertion_code` |  | string | Residue insertion code (PDB col 27, mmCIF `pdbx_PDB_ins_code`), e.g. "A" for residue 10A. Absent means no insertion code; a producer omits the PDB blank and the mmCIF `?` / `.` placeholders rather than writing them. Part of the residue identity (`chain_id`, `residue_seq`, `insertion_code`): residues 10 and 10A of one chain are distinct, and a consumer MUST NOT merge them. |
| `alt_loc` |  | string | Alternate-location indicator (PDB col 17, mmCIF `label_alt_id`), e.g. "A". Absent means the atom belongs to every conformer of its residue. Atoms of one residue with the same `atom_name` and different `alt_loc` are alternate positions of one site, each a separate entry of `atoms`; conformer X is the atoms with no `alt_loc` plus those with `alt_loc` X. |
| `occupancy` |  | number | Fractional site occupancy (PDB cols 55-60, mmCIF `occupancy`), 0 to 1. Absent means not recorded, not 1. Informational: a consumer MUST NOT drop or select atoms by occupancy unless its user asks it to. |
| `hetero` |  | boolean | True for an atom from a PDB `HETATM` record (mmCIF `group_PDB` `HETATM`): a ligand, ion, water or modified residue; false for an `ATOM` record of a standard polymer residue. Absent means not recorded. |

<a id="def-trajectoryatom"></a>

### `TrajectoryAtom`

Identity of one atom in the `atoms` list of a trajectory-family metadata payload. Positions live in the section's binary members, not here; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | yes | string |  |
| `atomic_number` | yes | integer |  |

<a id="def-trajectorymetadatacommon"></a>

### `TrajectoryMetadataCommon`

The keys that the metadata payloads of a `trajectory` (TrajectoryMetadataPayload) and of a `reaction.path` (ReactionPathMetadataPayload) share; each of those definitions extends this one. It names the atoms, in the atom order of `coords`, through at least one of `symbols`, `atomic_numbers` and `atoms`; per-frame arrays are in frame order. Typed-open: the keys named here are typed, and any other key is accepted and ignored by a consumer that does not understand it; see QVF spec § 5.5 (Trajectories, reactions, vibrations).

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbols` |  | array of string | Element symbol of each atom. |
| `atomic_numbers` |  | array of integer | Atomic number of each atom. |
| `atoms` |  | array of [`TrajectoryAtom`](#def-trajectoryatom) | Atom identities as objects, an alternative to `symbols` and `atomic_numbers`. When more than one of the three is present they MUST describe the same atoms. |
| `n_frames` |  | integer | Number of frames; equals the leading dimension of `coords`. |
| `energies` |  | array of number | Energy of each frame, in Hartree. When the section also carries the binary `energies` member, the two MUST agree within 1e-10 hartree. |
| `kind` |  | one of `"optimization"` \| `"irc"` \| `"md"` \| `"neb"` \| `"scan"` \| `"custom"` | What produced the frames: a geometry optimization, an intrinsic reaction coordinate, molecular dynamics, a nudged elastic band, a coordinate scan (relaxed or rigid), or something else. |
| `pbc` |  | array[3] of boolean | Per-axis periodicity of the frames: axis i is periodic iff pbc[i], as in the `structure` payload. Absent means the frames are molecular. For a `trajectory` it is REQUIRED when the section carries a `lattice` member, and a true entry requires that member. |
| `ensemble` |  | one of `"nve"` \| `"nvt"` \| `"npt"` \| `"nph"` \| `"custom"` | Thermodynamic ensemble of a molecular-dynamics run: constant N, V, E; N, V, T; N, p, T; N, p, H; or another. |
| `timestep_fs` |  | number | Time between consecutive frames, in fs. When the section has no `times` member, frame k is at k * timestep_fs. |
| `precision` |  | one of `"float64"` \| `"float32"` | Floating-point precision of the `coords` member; absent means float64. It MUST agree with that member's dtype: float32 coords require "float32" here. |
| `units` |  | object | Optional declaration of units: each key names a field of this payload or the role of a member of the section, each value a unit name. The units are fixed, and a declaration restates them: `energies` is `hartree`, `coords` is `angstrom`, and `times` and `timestep_fs` are `fs`; the `velocities` (Angstrom/fs) and `gradient` (hartree/bohr) members have no unit name and are not declared. See QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |

Fixed units: `energies` = `hartree`, `coords` = `angstrom`, `times` = `fs`, `timestep_fs` = `fs`.

<a id="def-valuewithunits"></a>

### `ValueWithUnits`

| Field | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | yes | number |  |
| `units` | yes | one of 25 values or one of `"Eh"` \| `"eV"` \| `"Hartree"` | Unit of `value`: a unit name, or one of the legacy spellings that archives written before the vocabulary carry. Producers write the unit name; see QVF spec § 4.3 (Units and numeric conventions). |
